2.11   Status Data Collection 
Status Data Collection enables the host to retrieve the current value of any Status Variable on demand, 
independent of the Event Notification mechanism described in Section 2.7. Status Variables are retrieved 
using S1F3 (Selected Equipment Status Request) and S1F4 (Selected Equipment Status Data), or 
discovered using S1F11/S1F12 as described in Section 2.9. 
2.11.1   Configuration Options 
Parameter Default Description 
MaxSVIDsPerRequest 100 Maximum number of SVIDs that may be requested in a single S1F3 
message. 
StatusRequestTimeout 5 s Maximum time the equipment will take to assemble and return an 
S1F4 response. 
2.11.2   Scenarios 
Scenario 1: Host Requests Selected Status Variables 
● Host sends S1F3 with SVID list = [2, 3, 10]. 
● Equipment responds with S1F4, returning the current values of MDLN, SOFTREV, and ControlState 
in the order requested. 
Scenario 2: Host Requests All Status Variables 
● Host sends S1F3 with an empty SVID list. 
● Equipment responds with S1F4, returning the current values of every defined Status Variable in SVID 
order. 
Scenario 3: Invalid SVID Requested 
● Host sends S1F3 with an SVID list containing an undefined SVID (e.g., 999).  
● Equipment returns S1F4 with the corresponding list item set to an item of length zero, indicating the 
SVID is unknown, per SEMI E5. 
2.12   Time Driven Trace 
Time Driven Trace allows the host to configure the equipment to periodically sample a set of variables at a 
fixed time interval and report the collected data. Trace configuration is performed using S2F23 (Trace 
Initialize Send), acknowledged with S2F24 (Trace Initialize Acknowledge). Trace data is reported using S6F1 
(Trace Data Send), acknowledged by the host with S6F2. The Shellback 200mm exposes the following Data 
Variables (DVIDs) for tracing: DVID 1 (ChamberPressure, F4, mTorr), DVID 2 (ChamberTemperat ure, 
F4, °C), and DVID 3 (RFForwardPower, F4, W). 
2.12.1   Configuration Options 
Parameter Default Description 
MaxConcurrentTraces 5 Maximum number of simultaneously active trace definitions (TRIDs). 
MaxTraceVariables 10 Maximum number of SVIDs/DVIDs that may be included in a single 
trace definition. 
MinSamplePeriod 100 ms Minimum allowed value for the trace sample period (REPGSZ). 
MaxTotalSamples 10000 Maximum number of samples that may be requested for a single 
trace (TOTSMP). 
2.12.2   Scenarios 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Scenario 1: Host Initiates a Trace 
● Host sends S2F23 with TRID = 1, DSPER = 1.000 s, TOTSMP = 60, REPGSZ = 1, and DVID list = [1, 
2] (ChamberPressure, ChamberTemperature). 
● Equipment validates the parameters, allocates a trace buffer, and responds with S2F24, TIAACK = 0 
(Accepted). 
● At each sample interval, the equipment sends S6F1 with TRID = 1 and the current values of DVID 1 
and DVID 2. The host responds with S6F2, ACK = 0. 
● After 60 samples have been collected, the equipment automatically terminates the trace.  
Scenario 2: Host Aborts an Active Trace 
● Host sends S2F23 referencing the existing TRID = 1 with TOTSMP = 0 to terminate the trace.  
● Equipment stops sampling, releases the trace buffer, and responds with S2F24, TIAACK = 0 
(Accepted). 
Scenario 3: Trace Request Rejected — Resource Limit Reached 
● Host sends S2F23 requesting a sixth concurrent trace while MaxConcurrentTraces (5) traces are 
already active. 
● Equipment responds with S2F24, TIAACK = 1 (Denied, too many trace definitions already active). No 
trace buffer is allocated. 
2.13   Alarm Management 
The Alarm Management capability provides reporting of equipment alarm conditions to the host. Alarms are 
identified by Alarm ID (ALID) and reported using S5F1 (Alarm Report Send), acknowledged by the host with 
S5F2 (Alarm Report Acknowledge). The host may enable or disable spontaneous reporting of individual 
alarms using S5F3 (Enable/Disable Alarm Send), acknowledged with S5F4, and may query currently active 
alarms using S5F5 (List Alarms Request) / S5F6 (List Alarms Data). 
2.13.1   Configuration Options 
Parameter Default Description 
AlarmReportingEnabled TRUE Master enable for spontaneous S5F1 alarm reporting. 
DefaultAlarmState Enabled Initial enable state for all defined ALIDs at equipment power-on. 
AlarmAutoClearEnabled TRUE If TRUE, alarms automatically transition to the clear state (ALCD bit 
7 = 0) once the underlying condition resolves. 
2.13.2   Variables 
Variable SVID Type Units Description 
ActiveAlarmCount 40 U2 — Number of alarms currently in the set (active) state. 
LastAlarmID 41 U4 — ALID of the most recently set or cleared alarm. 
2.13.3   Events 
The following Alarm IDs (ALIDs) are defined on the Shellback 200mm: 
ALID Alarm Text Category Description

limit. The active process is aborted. 
1002 Chamber Over-Temperature Error Process chamber temperature exceeded the safe 
operating limit. Heater outputs are disabled.

© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
1003 Vacuum Pump Fault Error The vacuum pump controller has reported a fault 
condition. 
2001 Wafer Transfer Timeout Warning The transfer robot did not complete a wafer transfer within 
the allotted time. 
2002 Spool Buffer Near Full Warning The spooling buffer (Section 2.19) has exceeded 90% of 
its capacity. 
2003 Equipment Constant Out of 
Range Attempted 
Warning The host attempted to set an Equipment Constant outside

2.13.4   Scenarios 
Scenario 1: Alarm Set 
● Chamber pressure exceeds the limit defined by ECID 3 (ChamberPressureSetpoint) plus a fixed 
safety margin. 
● Equipment sets ALID = 1001, increments ActiveAlarmCount (SVID 40), and sets LastAlarmID (SVID 
41) = 1001. 
● Equipment sends S5F1 with ALCD = Alarm Set, ALID = 1001, and ALTX = “Chamber Over -
Pressure”. 
● Host responds with S5F2, ACKC5 = 0 (Accepted). 
● The active process recipe is aborted and the Equipment Processing State (Section 2.4) transitions 
accordingly. 
Scenario 2: Alarm Cleared 
● The over-pressure condition resolves and AlarmAutoClearEnabled = TRUE. 
● Equipment decrements ActiveAlarmCount (SVID 40) and sends S5F1 with ALCD = Alarm Clear, ALID 
= 1001, ALTX = “Chamber Over-Pressure”. 
● Host responds with S5F2, ACKC5 = 0 (Accepted). 
Scenario 3: Host Disables Reporting for a Specific Alarm 
● Host sends S5F3 with ALED = FALSE and ALID list = [2003]. 
● Equipment disables spontaneous reporting for ALID 2003 and responds with S5F4, ACKC5 = 0 
(Accepted). 
● The underlying condition may still occur and affect ActiveAlarmCount, but no S5F1 is sent for ALID 
2003 while disabled. 
Scenario 4: Host Queries Currently Active Alarms 
● Host sends S5F5 with an empty ALID list (requesting all). 
● Equipment responds with S5F6, returning a list of (ALCD, ALID, ALTX) for every alarm currently in 
the set state.

2.16   Clock 
The Clock capability allows the host to read and set the equipment's internal date and time. Equipment time is 
used for event timestamps, alarm logs, and trace data. The host reads equipment time using S2F17 (Date 
and Time Request) / S2F18 (Date and Time Data), and sets equipment time using S2F31 (Date and Time Set 
Request) / S2F32 (Date and Time Set Acknowledge). 
2.16.1   Configuration Options 
Parameter Default Description 
ClockSyncOnConnect TRUE If TRUE, the equipment requests the current time from the 
host (S2F17) upon entering the COMMUNICATING state 
(Section 2.1). 
TimeFormat YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc Format of the TIME data item, per SEMI E5 (16-character 
ASCII, centisecond resolution). 
MaxClockDrift 5 s Maximum allowed drift between equipment and host time 
before a synchronization is forced. 
2.16.2   Variables 
Variable SVID Type Units Description 
Clock 60 ASCII — Current equipment date and time, formatted per 
TimeFormat. 
TimeZoneOffset 61 I2 min Offset of equipment local time from UTC, in minutes. 
2.16.3   Scenarios 
Scenario 1: Host Sets Equipment Time 
● Host sends S2F31 with TIME = “20240615143000.00”. 
● Equipment validates the format against TimeFormat and updates its internal clock.  
● Equipment responds with S2F32, TIACK = 0 (Accepted). 
Scenario 2: Equipment Requests Time from Host on Connect 
● Equipment enters the COMMUNICATING sub-state (Section 2.1) with ClockSyncOnConnect = 
TRUE. 
● Equipment sends S2F17 (Date and Time Request). 
● Host responds with S2F18, TIME = current host time. 
● If the difference between equipment time and host time exceeds MaxClockDrift, the equipment 
updates its internal clock to match. 
Scenario 3: Invalid Time Format Rejected 
● Host sends S2F31 with a TIME value that does not conform to the 16-character TimeFormat. 
● Equipment responds with S2F32, TIACK = 1 (Not accepted, format error). The equipment clock is 
unchanged. 
2.17   Error Messages 
The Shellback 200mm uses SECS Stream 9 to report message-level errors to the host. Stream 9 messages 
are sent by the equipment in response to host messages that cannot be processed due to format errors, 
unrecognized message identifiers, or message sequencing violations. Stream 9 messages are primary 
messages sent without reply and are used solely to notify the host of a communication -level problem; they do 
not affect equipment process state. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
The equipment does not send a Stream 9 message for application-level errors (for example, a rejected 
Remote Command). Those errors are reported through the appropriate reply message (e.g., HCACK in 
S2F42). 
2.17.1   Scenarios 
Scenario 1: Unrecognized Stream Received 
• Host sends a message with an unsupported Stream number (e.g., S12). 
• Equipment responds with S9F3 (Stream number not supported), including the message header of the 
offending message in the message body. 
• The original message is otherwise ignored. 
 
Scenario 2: Unrecognized Function Received 
• Host sends a supported Stream but an unrecognized Function (e.g., S1F99).  
• Equipment sends S9F5 (Function number not supported) with the message header of the offending 
message. 
 
Scenario 3: Illegal Data Format 
• Host sends a well-formed SECS-II message (recognized SxFy) but with a data structure that does not 
match the expected format (e.g., wrong data type for a variable). 
• Equipment sends S9F7 (Illegal data) with the first 10 bytes of the offending message body.  
• The equipment does not attempt to process the message. 
 
Scenario 4: Transaction Timeout 
• Equipment sends a primary message requiring a reply (W-bit set). 
• No reply is received within the T3 timeout period. 
• Equipment sends S9F9 (Transaction Timer Timeout) referencing the timed-out system bytes. 
• If the message was a collection event (S6F11), the event is re-queued for spooling if spooling is 
enabled (Section 2.19). 
  
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
2.18   Limits Monitoring 
Limits Monitoring allows the host to define upper and lower threshold values for selected Status Variables. 
When a variable's value crosses a defined limit, the equipment generates a Limits Monitoring event. Limits 
may be configured to define an inner zone (warning) and an outer zone (alarm) around a nominal value. This 
capability is defined in SEMI E30 as an Additional Capability. 
Limits are configured using S2F45 (Define Variable Limit Attributes) / S2F46 (Variable Limit Attribute 
Acknowledge), and queried using S2F47 (Variable Limit Attribute Request) / S2F48 (Variable Limit Attribute 
Data). Each limit definition includes an upper limit (UPPERDB), a lower limit (LOWERDB), an upper zone 
boundary (UPPERZONE), and a lower zone boundary (LOWERZONE). 
2.18.1   Variables to which Limits Monitoring may apply 
The following Status Variables are eligible for Limits Monitoring on the Shellback 200mm:  
SVID Name Type Units Description 
10 ControlState BINARY — Current control state value. 
20 ProcessingState ASCII — Equipment processing state string. 
30 ChamberPressure F4 mTorr Process chamber vacuum pressure. 
31 ChamberTemperature F4 °C Process chamber wall temperature. 
32 RFForwardPower F4 W RF generator forward power. 
33 RFReflectedPower F4 W RF generator reflected power. 
34 TargetBias F4 V Substrate bias voltage setpoint. 
35 DepositionRate F4 nm/s Real-time deposition rate from in-situ sensor. 
 
2.18.2   Limits Monitoring States & Transitions 
Each monitored variable independently tracks the following states: NORMAL (value is within all defined 
limits), UPPERWARNING (value has exceeded UPPERZONE but is below UPPERDB), LOWERWARNING 
(value has fallen below LOWERZONE but is above LOWERDB), UPPERALARM (value has exceeded 
UPPERDB), and LOWERALARM (value has fallen below LOWERDB). 
Transitions between states generate the LimitZoneChange event (CEID 600). If a variable is not configured 
with a limit definition for a given zone, that zone transition is not reported.  
2.18.3   Configuration Options 
Parameter Default Description 
LimitsMonitoringEnabled TRUE Master enable for Limits Monitoring event generation. 
MaxLimitDefinitions 20 Maximum number of variable limit definitions that may be active 
simultaneously. 
LimitHysteresis 0.0 Hysteresis band applied to all limit transitions to prevent chattering. 
Units match the monitored variable.

Variable SVID Type Units Description 
LimitViolationCount 70 U2 — Cumulative number of limit violation events generated since 
last equipment power-on. 
ActiveLimitCount 71 U2 — Number of variables currently outside their defined Normal 
zone. 
 
2.18.5   Events 
Event Name CEID Description 
LimitZoneChange 600 A monitored variable has transitioned between limit zones (e.g., NORMAL to 
UPPERWARNING, or UPPERWARNING to UPPERALARM). 
AllLimitsNormal 601 All previously violated limits have returned to the NORMAL state. 
 
2.18.6   Scenarios 
Scenario 1: Host Defines Limits for Chamber Pressure 
• Host sends S2F45 with SVID = 30 (ChamberPressure), UPPERDB = 15.0, UPPERZONE = 12.0, 
LOWERDB = 0.5, LOWERZONE = 1.0, units = mTorr. 
• Equipment validates the range definitions and stores the limit attributes. 
• Equipment responds with S2F46, LEACK = 0 (Accepted). 
 
Scenario 2: Limit Zone Violation Detected 
• ChamberPressure value rises from 8.0 to 12.5 mTorr, crossing UPPERZONE = 12.0.  
• Equipment transitions variable state to UPPERWARNING. 
• Equipment increments LimitViolationCount (SVID 70) and sends S6F11 with CEID = 600 
(LimitZoneChange), reporting the SVID, new zone state, and current variable value.  
 
Scenario 3: Host Queries Current Limit Attributes 
• Host sends S2F47 with SVID list = [30, 31]. 
• Equipment responds with S2F48, returning the stored limit attributes for ChamberPressure and 
ChamberTemperature. 
 
Scenario 4: Host Removes a Limit Definition 
• Host sends S2F45 with SVID = 30 and an empty limit attribute list. 
• Equipment removes the limit definition for ChamberPressure. The variable is no longer monitored.  
• Equipment responds with S2F46, LEACK = 0 (Accepted).

2.19   Spooling 
Spooling provides reliable delivery of SECS messages during periods when the host communication link is 
unavailable. When spooling is enabled and the equipment is in the NOT COMMUNICATING state (Section 
2.1), outgoing primary messages that would otherwise be discarded are stored in a local spool buffer. Upon 
re-establishing communication, the equipment delivers spooled messages to the host in the order they were 
generated. This capability is defined in SEMI E30 as an Additional Capability.  
Spooling applies to equipment-originated primary messages only: principally collection event reports (S6F11) 
and alarm notifications (S5F1). The host activates and deactivates spooling using S2F43 (Reset Spooling 
Streams and Functions) / S2F44 (Reset Spooling Acknowledge). The equipment acknowledges spooled 
message delivery using S6F24 (Spool Transmit Acknowledge). 
2.19.1   Spooling Sequence 
The spooling operational sequence is as follows: 
• Host activates spooling for the desired streams and functions using S2F43.  
• While the equipment is in the COMMUNICATING state, messages are delivered normally without 
spooling. 
• When communication is lost (transition to NOT COMMUNICATING), the equipment begins spooling 
qualifying outgoing primary messages to the local spool buffer. 
• When the COMMUNICATING state is re-entered, the equipment notifies the host that a spool exists 
by sending S6F23 (Request Spooled Data) prior to delivering any new live messages.  
• The host requests spool delivery by sending S6F23 (if necessary to initiate) or the equipment sends 
spooled messages beginning from the oldest entry. 
• Each spooled message is delivered and individually acknowledged by the host (S6F24, ACKC6 = 0).  
• Upon successful delivery of all spooled messages, the spool buffer is cleared. 
 
2.19.2   Spooling States & Transitions 
The spool subsystem operates as a concurrent state machine independent of the main communication and 
control state machines. 
Trans. From State To State Trigger / Condition 
S1 SPOOL_INACTIVE SPOOL_ACTIVE Host sends S2F43 enabling spooling for at least one 
stream/function. 
S2 SPOOL_ACTIVE SPOOL_INACTIVE Host sends S2F43 with an empty stream/function list, 
disabling all spooling. 
S3 SPOOL_ACTIVE SPOOL_TRANSMIT Communication re-established; spool buffer contains one 
or more messages. 
S4 SPOOL_TRANSMIT SPOOL_ACTIVE All spooled messages acknowledged; spool buffer 
empty. 
S5 SPOOL_TRANSMIT SPOOL_PURGE Host requests spool purge via S6F23 with purge flag set. 
S6 SPOOL_PURGE SPOOL_ACTIVE Spool buffer cleared following host purge request. 
 
2.19.3   Configuration Options 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Parameter Default Description 
SpoolingEnabled FALSE Master enable for spooling. Must be set to TRUE before S2F43 
activation takes effect. 
SpoolBufferSize 500 Maximum number of messages that may be held in the spool buffer 
simultaneously. 
SpoolOverflowAction DISCARD Action when spool buffer is full: DISCARD (oldest messages 
discarded), HALT (no new messages accepted until space available). 
SpoolTransmitRate 10 msg/s Maximum rate at which spooled messages are delivered after re-
connection. 
SpoolRetentionPeriod 72 h Maximum time spooled messages are retained. Messages older than 
this are automatically purged. 
 
2.19.4   Variables 
Variable SVID Type Units Description 
SpoolingState 80 ASCII — Current spooling state: INACTIVE, ACTIVE, TRANSMITTING, 
or PURGING. 
SpoolCount 81 U4 — Number of messages currently stored in the spool buffer. 
SpoolCapacity 82 U4 — Maximum number of messages the spool buffer can hold 
(SpoolBufferSize). 
SpoolOldestAge 83 U4 min Age of the oldest message in the spool buffer in minutes. Zero 
if spool is empty. 
 
2.19.5   Events 
Event Name CEID Description 
SpoolActivated 700 The host has enabled spooling via S2F43; the spool subsystem is now 
active. 
SpoolDeactivated 701 Spooling has been fully disabled via S2F43. 
SpoolTransmitStarted 702 Delivery of spooled messages to the host has begun following 
communication re-establishment. 
SpoolTransmitComplete 703 All spooled messages have been successfully delivered. Spool buffer is now 
empty. 
SpoolBufferNearFull 704 Spool buffer occupancy has reached 90% of SpoolBufferSize (alarm 2002 
also raised). 
SpoolMessagePurged 705 One or more spooled messages have been discarded due to buffer overflow 
or retention timeout. 
 
2.19.6   Scenarios 
Scenario 1: Host Activates Spooling 
• Host sends S2F43 with stream/function list = [(S5, F1), (S6, F11)] to enable spooling for alarm reports 
and collection event reports. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
• Equipment enables spooling for those message types and responds with S2F44, RSPACK = 0 
(Accepted). 
• Equipment sends S6F11 with CEID = 700 (SpoolActivated). 
 
Scenario 2: Spool Accumulation During Communication Loss 
• The TCP connection between equipment and host is lost. Equipment transitions to NOT 
COMMUNICATING. 
• During the outage, a wafer process completes. The equipment would normally send S6F11 events 
and S5F1 alarm messages. 
• Because spooling is active, these messages are written to the spool buffer. SpoolCount (SVID 81) 
increments for each stored message. 
• If SpoolCount reaches 90% of SpoolCapacity, the equipment sends CEID 704 (SpoolBufferNearFull) 
to the local event log (cannot send to host while offline) and raises alarm 2002.  
 
Scenario 3: Spool Delivery After Re-connection 
• TCP connection is restored. Equipment successfully enters the COMMUNICATING sub -state. 
• Equipment sends S6F23 to the host to signal that spooled messages are available.  
• Host acknowledges readiness and the equipment begins delivering spooled messages in FIFO order 
at the SpoolTransmitRate. 
• The host acknowledges each S6F11 or S5F1 with the appropriate reply (S6F12 or S5F2). The 
equipment sends S6F24 after each acknowledged message. 
• When SpoolCount reaches 0, the equipment sends S6F11 with CEID = 703 
(SpoolTransmitComplete). 
 
Scenario 4: Host Purges the Spool 
• Host sends S6F23 with the purge flag set. 
• Equipment discards all spooled messages, resets SpoolCount to 0, and sends S6F11 with CEID = 
705 (SpoolMessagePurged). 
• Equipment transitions back to SPOOL_ACTIVE state.

3   SECS Message Detail 
This chapter provides detailed specifications for each SECS-II message supported by the Shellback 200mm. 
Messages are organized by Stream number. For each message, the direction (Host -to-Equipment H→E, 
Equipment-to-Host E→H, or bidirectional), the reply requirement, and the data item structure are described. 
Data item types referenced in this chapter are fully defined in Chapter 4 (Data Item Dictionary). Item format 
codes follow the SEMI E5 convention: ASCII = A, Binary = B, Boolean = BOOLEAN, Unsigned Integer = 
U1/U2/U4/U8, Signed Integer = I1/I2/I4/I8, Float = F4/F8, List = L.

3.3   Stream 1: Equipment Status 
Stream 1 messages provide equipment status and identification information. The host uses these messages 
to determine equipment identity, retrieve the values of Status Variables, and manage the communication 
session. 
S1F1 / S1F2 — Are You There / On-Line Data 
Direction: H→E (S1F1), E→H (S1F2).  Reply: Required. 
S1F1 is sent by the host to confirm the equipment is communicating. The equipment responds with S1F2 
containing its model number and software revision. The equipment may also send S1F1 as a communication 
confirmation after entering the COMMUNICATING state. 
Message Item Format Description 
S1F1 (H→E) (Header only) — No message body. W-bit set. 
S1F2 (E→H) L [2] List Two-element list. 
 MDLN A[20] Equipment Model Number. Fixed: "SB200". 
 SOFTREV A[20] Software Revision. Example: "3.2.1". 
 
S1F3 / S1F4 — Selected Equipment Status Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S1F3), E→H (S1F4).  Reply: Required. 
The host sends a list of SVIDs to retrieve. If the SVID list is empty, the equipment returns all defined Status 
Variables. For unrecognized SVIDs, the corresponding list item in S1F4 is returned with zero length.  
Message Item Format Description 
S1F3 (H→E) L [n] List List of n SVID values to retrieve. 
 SVID U4 Status Variable ID. Repeat for each desired variable. Empty 
list = request all. 
S1F4 (E→H) L [n] List List of n variable values, in the same order as the request. 
 SV (any) Value of the corresponding Status Variable. Zero-length item 
if SVID is undefined. 
 
S1F11 / S1F12 — Status Variable Namelist Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S1F11), E→H (S1F12).  Reply: Required. 
Allows the host to discover defined Status Variables and their names and units. An empty SVID list in S1F11 
requests all defined Status Variables. 
Message Item Format Description 
S1F11 (H→E) L [n] List List of SVIDs to query. Empty list = all SVIDs. 
 SVID U4 Status Variable ID to query. 
S1F12 (E→H) L [n] List List of n entries, one per SVID in request order. 
 L [3] List Per-SVID entry. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Message Item Format Description 
   SVID U4 Status Variable ID. 
   SVNAME A[n] Symbolic name of the Status Variable. 
   UNITS A[n] Engineering units string per SEMI E5 (empty if 
dimensionless). 
 
S1F13 / S1F14 — Establish Communications Request / Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S1F13), H→E (S1F14).  Reply: Required. 
Sent by the equipment upon entering NOT COMMUNICATING state to initiate session establishment. The 
host responds with S1F14 to confirm the session. COMMACK = 0 indicates acceptance; non -zero values 
indicate refusal. 
Message Item Format Description 
S1F13 (E→H) L [2] List Two-element list. 
 MDLN A[20] Equipment Model Number. 
 SOFTREV A[20] Software Revision. 
S1F14 (H→E) L [2] List Two-element list. 
 COMMACK B[1] 0 = Accepted; 1 = Denied, Try Again; 2 = Denied, Already 
Connected. 
 L [2] List Echo of MDLN and SOFTREV from S1F13. 
 
S1F15 / S1F16 — Request OFF-LINE / OFF-LINE Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S1F15), E→H (S1F16).  Reply: Required. 
The host requests that the equipment transition to the EQUIPMENT OFFLINE control state. OFLACK = 0 
indicates the equipment has accepted the request and will initiate the offline transition. The equipment will 
send CEID 100 (EquipmentOffline) upon completing the transition. 
Message Item Format Description 
S1F15 (H→E) (Header only) — No body. W-bit set. 
S1F16 (E→H) OFLACK B[1] 0 = Acknowledged, will go offline; 1 = Denied. 
 
S1F17 / S1F18 — Request ON-LINE / ON-LINE Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S1F17), E→H (S1F18).  Reply: Required. 
The host requests that the equipment transition from the EQUIPMENT OFFLINE or ATTEMPT ONLINE state 
to an online sub-state. ONLACK indicates whether the request is accepted and which online sub -state is 
entered. Value 0 = Accepted (Online/Remote); 1 = Accepted (Online/Local); 2 = Denied. 
Message Item Format Description 
S1F17 (H→E) (Header only) — No body. W-bit set. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Message Item Format Description 
S1F18 (E→H) ONLACK B[1] 0 = Online/Remote; 1 = Online/Local; 2 = Denied.

3.4   Stream 2: Equipment Control and Diagnostics 
Stream 2 messages provide host control of equipment constants, traces, event reports, remote commands, 
spooling, and limits monitoring. Stream 2 also includes clock management messages.  
S2F13 / S2F14 — Equipment Constant Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S2F13), E→H (S2F14).  Reply: Required. 
Retrieves the current value of one or more Equipment Constants. An empty ECID list in S2F13 returns all 
defined ECs. 
Message Item Format Description 
S2F13 (H→E) L [n] List List of ECIDs to retrieve. Empty = all. 
 ECID U4 Equipment Constant ID. 
S2F14 (E→H) L [n] List EC values in request order. 
 ECV (any) Current value of the Equipment Constant. Type matches EC 
definition. 
 
S2F15 / S2F16 — New Equipment Constant Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S2F15), E→H (S2F16).  Reply: Required. 
The host sends new values for one or more Equipment Constants. Each entry includes the ECID and the new 
value. EAC codes: 0 = Accepted; 1 = Invalid ECID; 2 = Invalid data; 3 = Not allowed at this time.  
Message Item Format Description 
S2F15 (H→E) L [n] List List of n EC update entries. 
 L [2] List Per-EC entry. 
   ECID U4 Equipment Constant ID. 
   ECV (any) New value for the Equipment Constant. 
S2F16 (E→H) EAC B[1] Equipment Acknowledge Code: 0=OK, 1=invalid ECID, 
2=invalid data, 3=busy. 
 
S2F17 / S2F18 — Date and Time Request / Data 
Direction: Bidirectional.  Reply: Required. 
Either the host or the equipment may send S2F17 to request the current date and time from the other party. 
The response S2F18 contains the TIME data item formatted per the TimeFormat Equipment Constant 
(Section 2.16). 
Message Item Format Description 
S2F17 (Header only) — No body. W-bit set. 
S2F18 TIME A[16] Current date/time: YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc (centisecond 
resolution).

Configures a periodic variable trace. TIAACK codes: 0 = OK; 1 = Too many traces; 2 = Invalid TRID; 3 =

S2F37 / S2F38 — Enable/Disable Event Report / Acknowledge

S2F45 / S2F46 — Define Variable Limit Attributes / Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S2F45), E→H (S2F46).  Reply: Required. 
Defines or modifies limit zone boundaries for one or more Status Variables (Section 2.18). Sending a limit 
definition with an empty zone list removes all limits for that SVID. LEACK codes: 0 = OK; 1 = Invalid SVID; 2 = 
Invalid limits; 3 = Cannot perform now. 
Message Item Format Description 
S2F45 (H→E) L [2] List Limit definition message. 
 DATAID U4 Data ID. 
 L [n] List List of n per-SVID limit definitions. 
 L [2] List Per-SVID entry. 
   SVID U4 Status Variable ID. 
   L [m] List List of m limit zone definitions (empty = remove all limits for 
SVID). 
   L [4] List Per-zone entry. 
     UPPERDB (F4) Upper alarm limit value. 
     LOWERDB (F4) Lower alarm limit value. 
     UPPERZONE (F4) Upper warning zone boundary. 
     
LOWERZONE (F4) Lower warning zone boundary. 
S2F46 (E→H) LEACK B[1] Limit Attribute Acknowledge code. 
 
S2F47 / S2F48 — Variable Limit Attribute Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S2F47), E→H (S2F48).  Reply: Required. 
Retrieves current limit zone definitions for specified SVIDs. An empty SVID list returns limit attributes for all 
SVIDs that have active limit definitions. 
Message Item Format Description 
S2F47 (H→E) L [n] List List of SVIDs to query. Empty = all. 
 SVID U4 Status Variable ID. 
S2F48 (E→H) L [n] List Response list, one entry per queried SVID. 
 L [2] List Per-SVID response entry. 
   SVID U4 Status Variable ID. 
   Limit zones L[m] Limit zone definitions as configured (same structure as 
S2F45).

3.5   Stream 5: Exception Handling 
Stream 5 messages manage alarm reporting. The equipment uses S5F1 to send alarm notifications 
spontaneously. The host uses S5F3 to control which alarms generate spontaneous reports, and S5F5 to 
query currently active alarms. 
S5F1 / S5F2 — Alarm Report Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S5F1), H→E (S5F2).  Reply: Required. 
Sent by the equipment when an alarm transitions to Set or Clear state. ALCD bit 7: 1 = Alarm Set; 0 = Alarm 
Cleared. Lower 7 bits indicate alarm category (see Section 2.13). ACKC5 = 0 means accepted.  
Message Item Format Description 
S5F1 (E→H) L [3] List Alarm notification. 
 ALCD B[1] Alarm Code: bit 7 = 1 (Set) or 0 (Clear); lower 7 bits = 
category. 
 ALID U4 Alarm ID as defined in Section 2.13. 
 ALTX A[40] Alarm text string. Maximum 40 characters. 
S5F2 (H→E) ACKC5 B[1] 0 = Accepted. 
 
S5F3 / S5F4 — Enable/Disable Alarm Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S5F3), E→H (S5F4).  Reply: Required. 
Controls spontaneous alarm reporting for specified ALIDs. An empty ALID list with ALED = TRUE enables all 
defined alarms; with ALED = FALSE disables all. ACKC5 = 0 means accepted; 1 = invalid ALID.  
Message Item Format Description 
S5F3 (H→E) L [2] List Enable/disable request. 
 ALED BOOLEAN TRUE = Enable; FALSE = Disable. 
 ALID list L[n] List of ALIDs. Empty = all defined alarms. 
S5F4 (E→H) ACKC5 B[1] Alarm Acknowledge: 0 = Accepted; 1 = Invalid ALID. 
 
S5F5 / S5F6 — List Alarms Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S5F5), E→H (S5F6).  Reply: Required. 
The host queries the set of alarms that are currently active (Set state). An empty ALID list in S5F5 requests all 
currently active alarms. 
Message Item Format Description 
S5F5 (H→E) L [n] List List of ALIDs to check. Empty = return all active alarms. 
 ALID U4 Alarm ID to query. 
S5F6 (E→H) L [n] List List of currently active alarms matching the request. 
 L [3] List Per-alarm entry. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Message Item Format Description 
   ALCD B[1] Alarm Code (as in S5F1; always Set here). 
   ALID U4 Alarm ID. 
   ALTX A[40] Alarm text. 
  
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
3.6   Stream 6: Data Collection 
Stream 6 messages are the primary mechanism for equipment-to-host data delivery. This includes event 
reports, trace data, and spooled message delivery. 
S6F1 / S6F2 — Trace Data Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S6F1), H→E (S6F2).  Reply: Required. 
Delivers a group of trace samples as configured by S2F23. Each S6F1 message contains REPGSZ samples. 
ACKC6 = 0 means accepted. 
Message Item Format Description 
S6F1 (E→H) L [4] List Trace data message. 
 TRID U4 Trace ID corresponding to the S2F23 definition. 
 SMPLN U4 Sample number of the first sample in this message. 
 STIME A[16] Timestamp of the first sample (YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc). 
 L [n] List List of n samples (n = REPGSZ). 
 L [m] List Per-sample entry: list of m variable values in SVID/DVID 
order. 
S6F2 (H→E) ACKC6 B[1] 0 = Accepted. 
 
S6F11 / S6F12 — Event Report Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S6F11), H→E (S6F12).  Reply: Required. 
The primary event notification message. Delivered when a Collection Event fires and event reporting is 
enabled for the CEID. The message body includes the CEID and all linked report data as configured by 
S2F33/S2F35. ACKC6 = 0 means accepted. 
Message Item Format Description 
S6F11 (E→H) L [3] List Event report. 
 DATAID U4 Data ID (unique per message for spooling correlation). 
 CEID U4 Collection Event ID that triggered this report. 
 L [n] List List of n report entries (one per linked RPTID). 
 L [2] List Per-report entry. 
   RPTID U4 Report ID. 
   L [m] List Variable values in the order defined in the report. 
S6F12 (H→E) ACKC6 B[1] 0 = Accepted; 1 = Too many reports active; 2 = No such 
object. 
 
S6F13 / S6F14 — Annotated Event Report Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S6F13), H→E (S6F14).  Reply: Required. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Functionally identical to S6F11/S6F12, but each variable value in the report body is preceded by its VID, 
providing self-describing message content without requiring the host to maintain the RPTID -to-VID mapping. 
The equipment sends S6F13 only when the host has specifically requested annotated reporting. 
 
S6F19 / S6F20 — Collection Event Namelist Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S6F19), E→H (S6F20).  Reply: Required. 
Allows the host to discover all defined Collection Events and their associated VIDs. An empty CEID list in 
S6F19 requests all defined CEIDs. 
Message Item Format Description 
S6F19 (H→E) L [n] List List of CEIDs to query. Empty = all. 
 CEID U4 Collection Event ID. 
S6F20 (E→H) L [n] List Response list. 
 L [3] List Per-CEID entry. 
   CEID U4 Collection Event ID. 
   CENAME A[n] Symbolic name of the Collection Event. 
   VID list L[m] List of SVIDs and DVIDs associated with this event. 
 
S6F23 / S6F24 — Request Spooled Data / Spool Transmit Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S6F23) or H→E (S6F23).  Reply: S6F24 (H→E) per spooled message.  
S6F23 is sent by the equipment to notify the host that spooled messages are available after re -connection. 
The host may also send S6F23 to request purge of the spool buffer. ACKC6 in S6F24 = 0 confirms delivery of 
each spooled message. RSPACK = 0 means purge accepted. 
  
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL

3.7   Stream 7: Process Program Management 
Stream 7 messages provide host management of Process Programs (recipes) stored on the Shellback 
200mm. The equipment supports upload, download, deletion, and directory listing of Process Programs.  
S7F3 / S7F4 — Process Program Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S7F3), E→H (S7F4).  Reply: Required. 
Host downloads a Process Program to the equipment. ACKC7 codes: 0 = Accepted; 1 = Permission not 
granted; 2 = Length error; 3 = Matrix overflow; 4 = PPID not found; 5 = Mode unsupported; 6 = Command not 
valid at this time. 
Message Item Format Description 
S7F3 (H→E) L [2] List Process program download. 
 PPID A[64] Process Program ID (recipe name). 
 PPBODY A[n] Process Program body (ASCII text, max MaxPPSize bytes). 
S7F4 (E→H) ACKC7 B[1] Process Program Acknowledge code. 
 
S7F5 / S7F6 — Process Program Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S7F5), E→H (S7F6).  Reply: Required. 
Host requests upload of a stored Process Program. ACKC7 = 4 in S7F6 indicates the PPID was not found.  
Message Item Format Description 
S7F5 (H→E) PPID A[64] PPID of the Process Program to retrieve. 
S7F6 (E→H) L [2] List Process program upload response. 
 PPID A[64] Echo of the requested PPID. 
 PPBODY A[n] Process Program body. Zero-length if PPID not found. 
 
S7F17 / S7F18 — Delete Process Program Send / Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S7F17), E→H (S7F18).  Reply: Required. 
Deletes one or more named Process Programs from equipment storage. ACKC7 = 0 means all deletions 
were successful; 1 = permission not granted; 4 = one or more PPIDs not found.  
Message Item Format Description 
S7F17 (H→E) L [n] List List of n PPIDs to delete. 
 PPID A[64] Process Program ID to delete. 
S7F18 (E→H) ACKC7 B[1] 0 = All deleted; 1 = Not permitted; 4 = PPID not found. 
 
S7F19 / S7F20 — Current EPPD Request / Data 
Direction: H→E (S7F19), E→H (S7F20).  Reply: Required. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Retrieves the directory of Process Programs stored on the equipment. The response is a list of all currently 
stored PPIDs. 
Message Item Format Description 
S7F19 (H→E) (Header only) — No body. W-bit set. 
S7F20 (E→H) L [n] List List of n PPIDs currently stored. 
 PPID A[64] Process Program ID.

3.8   Stream 9: System Errors 
Stream 9 messages are sent by the equipment to report protocol-level errors to the host. These messages 
are primary messages sent without reply (W-bit not set). They do not affect equipment process state and 
serve only as diagnostic notifications. 
Message Name Trigger 
S9F1 Unrecognized Device ID Message received with an unrecognized Device ID. 
S9F3 Unrecognized Stream Type Message received with an unsupported Stream number. 
S9F5 Unrecognized Function Type Supported Stream but unsupported Function number received. 
S9F7 Illegal Data Recognized SxFy received but with a malformed data structure. 
S9F9 Transaction Timer Timeout Equipment sent a W-bit primary message and did not receive a 
reply within T3. 
S9F11 Data Too Long Received message body exceeds the maximum allowed block 
size. 
S9F13 Conversation Timeout Multi-block conversation did not complete within T4 (if 
applicable). 
 
Each S9 message carries a message header block as the body, providing enough context for the host to 
identify the offending transaction. S9F9 includes the system bytes of the timed -out transaction. No reply is 
expected from the host for any Stream 9 message. 
3.9   Stream 10: Terminal Services 
Stream 10 messages implement the Equipment Terminal Services capability (Section 2.15). They enable text 
messaging between the host and the equipment operator terminal (HMI). 
S10F1 / S10F2 — Terminal Request / Acknowledge 
Direction: E→H (S10F1), H→E (S10F2).  Reply: Required. 
The operator on the equipment HMI sends a free-text message to the host. The host acknowledges with 
S10F2. ACK10 = 0 means accepted and displayed. 
Message Item Format Description 
S10F1 (E→H) L [2] List Operator terminal message. 
 TID B[1] Terminal ID. 0 = primary HMI display. 
 TEXT A[n] Free-text message from the operator. 
S10F2 (H→E) ACK10 B[1] 0 = Accepted; 1 = Message not displayed. 
 
S10F3 / S10F4 — Terminal Display, Single / Acknowledge 
Direction: H→E (S10F3), E→H (S10F4).  Reply: Required. 
The host sends a text message for display on the equipment HMI. Message length is limited to 
MaxDisplayMessageLength (Section 2.15). ACK10 codes: 0 = Accepted and displayed; 1 = Not accepted, 
terminal not available; 2 = Not accepted, no such terminal. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Message Item Format Description 
S10F3 (H→E) L [2] List Host display request. 
 TID B[1] Terminal ID. 0 = primary HMI display. 
 TEXT A[n] Message text to display. Maximum 
MaxDisplayMessageLength characters. 
S10F4 (E→H) ACK10 B[1] 0 = Displayed; 1 = Terminal not available; 2 = No such 
terminal. 
 
Note: The Shellback 200mm supports TID = 0 (primary HMI display) only. Messages directed to other 
terminal IDs are rejected with ACK10 = 2.

4   Data Item Dictionary 
This chapter defines all SECS-II data items used in the Shellback 200mm host interface. Data items are 
atomic pieces of information transferred within SECS-II messages. Each item is identified by a symbolic name 
and has a defined format code that specifies its data type and encoding as defined in SEMI E5. Data items 
appear as leaf nodes in the nested List structures of SECS-II message bodies. 
 
Data items are listed alphabetically. Where an item carries a defined set of enumerated values, the valid 
values and their meanings are described. For items whose values are equipment -specific (such as variable 
IDs and event IDs), the values are defined in this document's respective section or in the Variable Item 
Dictionary (Chapter 5). 
 
4.1   Data Types 
The following SECS-II data types are used in messages described in this document. All multi -byte integer and 
floating-point types are transmitted in big-endian (most-significant-byte first) byte order as required by SEMI 
E5. 
 
Format Code Type Description Max 
Length 
A ASCII Variable-length character string. Characters are 7-bit 
ASCII encoded in 8-bit bytes. Length is in bytes. 
1024 bytes 
B Binary Sequence of unsigned 8-bit byte values. Used for 
acknowledge codes, alarm codes, and flag fields. 
— 
BOOLEAN Boolean Single byte: 0x00 = FALSE, any non-zero = TRUE. 1 byte 
U1 Unsigned Int 1 8-bit unsigned integer. Range 0 to 255. 1 byte 
U2 Unsigned Int 2 16-bit unsigned integer, big-endian. Range 0 to 
65,535. 
2 bytes 
U4 Unsigned Int 4 32-bit unsigned integer, big-endian. Range 0 to 
4,294,967,295. 
4 bytes 
U8 Unsigned Int 8 64-bit unsigned integer, big-endian. Range 0 to 2^64 
− 1. 
8 bytes 
I1 Signed Int 1 8-bit two's-complement signed integer. Range −128 
to 127. 
1 byte 
I2 Signed Int 2 16-bit two's-complement signed integer, big-endian. 
Range −32,768 to 32,767. 
2 bytes 
I4 Signed Int 4 32-bit two's-complement signed integer, big-endian. 
Range −2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647. 
4 bytes 
I8 Signed Int 8 64-bit two's-complement signed integer, big-endian. 8 bytes 
F4 Float 4 32-bit IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point, big-
endian. 
4 bytes 
F8 Float 8 64-bit IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point, big-
endian. 
8 bytes 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Format Code Type Description Max 
Length 
L List Structured container of zero or more SECS-II items. 
A List item has its own format byte and length 
specifying the number of elements (not bytes). Lists 
may be nested. 
— 
 
NOTE  The List (L) item is a container, not a scalar type. Its length field in the SECS-II encoding specifies the number 
of elements, not a byte count. Lists may be nested to arbitrary depth; however, practical implementations limit nesting 
depth for stack efficiency.

Format:  B[1] 
Online Acknowledge Code. Returned in S1F18 in response to the host's S1F17 online request. 
Value Meaning 
0 Online — Remote control state 
1 Online — Local control state 
2 Denied — unable to go online 
 
 
PPBODY 
Format:  A[n] 
Process Program Body. ASCII text content of a Process Program (recipe). Maximum size is bounded by the MaxPPSize 
Equipment Constant. Exchanged in S7F3 (download) and S7F6 (upload). The internal format is a line-oriented ASCII text 
format described in the process recipe documentation. 
 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
PPID 
Format:  A[64] 
Process Program ID. ASCII string uniquely identifying a Process Program (recipe) stored on the equipment. Maximum 
length: 64 characters. Used in S7F3 (download), S7F5 (upload request), S7F6 (upload data), S7F17 (delete), 
S7F19/S7F20 (directory). PPID values are case-sensitive. Valid characters: alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen, period. 
 
RCMD 
Format:  A[n] 
Remote Command. ASCII string identifying a Remote Command in the S2F41/S2F42 exchange. Valid RCMD values are 
listed in Section 2.6.5. Maximum length: 64 characters. 
 
REPGSZ 
Format:  U4 
Report Group Size. The number of trace samples to accumulate per S6F1 Trace Data Send message. Sent in S2F23. 
Must be greater than zero and must not exceed TOTSMP. 
 
RPTID 
Format:  U4 
Report ID. A 32-bit unsigned integer identifying a host-defined data report. Used in S2F33 (define), S2F34 (acknowledge), 
S2F35 (link), S6F11/S6F12 (event report). Predefined RPTIDs are listed in Section 2.8.1. 
 
RSPACK 
Format:  B[1] 
Reset Spooling Acknowledge Code. Returned in S2F44. 
Value Meaning 
0 Accepted — spooling streams/functions updated 
1 Spooling disabled by equipment configuration (SpoolingEnabled = FALSE) 
2 Invalid stream or function in the request 
 
 
SFCD 
Format:  B[1] 
Stream Function Code. Identifies a SECS-II message by its 1-byte stream/function code when used in certain diagnostic 
contexts. 
 
SMPLN 
Format:  U4 
Sample Number. The sequential index of the first sample in a Trace Data Send (S6F1) message, relative to the start of 
the trace. The first sample is index 1. 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
 
SOFTREV 
Format:  A[20] 
Software Revision. ASCII string identifying the equipment controller software version. Example: "3.2.1". Sent in S1F2, 
S1F13, and S1F14. 
 
STIME 
Format:  A[16] 
Sample Time. Timestamp of the first sample in a S6F1 Trace Data Send message. Format: YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc (16-
character ASCII, centisecond resolution). All timestamps are in equipment local time unless TimeZoneOffset (SVID 61) 
indicates otherwise. 
 
STYPE 
Format:  U1 
Stream Type. The SECS-II stream number (1–10) of a message. Used in S2F43 (spool stream/function definition) and in 
S9 error message bodies. 
 
SV 
Format:  (any) 
Status Variable Value. The current value of a Status Variable, returned in S1F4. The data type matches the Status 
Variable definition. If an unrecognized SVID is requested, the corresponding S1F4 list entry is a zero-length item. 
 
SVID 
Format:  U4 
Status Variable ID. A 32-bit unsigned integer uniquely identifying a Status Variable. Used in S1F3 (request), S1F4 (data), 
S1F11 (namelist request), S1F12 (namelist data), S2F35 (link as VID), S2F45/S2F47 (limits monitoring). 
 
SVNAME 
Format:  A[n] 
Status Variable Name. ASCII string providing a human-readable symbolic name for a Status Variable. Maximum length: 
64 characters. Returned in S1F12 (Status Variable Namelist Data). 
 
TEXT 
Format:  A[n] 
Display Text. Free-form ASCII message text for operator display or operator-to-host communication. Used in S10F1 
(Terminal Request from operator) and S10F3 (Terminal Display from host). Maximum length is bounded by 
MaxDisplayMessageLength (Section 2.15). 
 
TIAACK 
Format:  B[1] 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Trace Initialize Acknowledge Code. Returned in S2F24. 
Value Meaning 
0 Accepted 
1 Too many concurrent traces active 
2 Invalid TRID — already in use 
3 Invalid DSPER — format error or period too short 
4 Invalid TOTSMP — zero or exceeds maximum 
5 Invalid REPGSZ — exceeds TOTSMP or is zero 
6 Invalid SVID/DVID — one or more unrecognized variable IDs 
 
 
TID 
Format:  B[1] 
Terminal ID. Identifies the HMI terminal for S10 message routing. The Shellback 200mm supports TID = 0 only (primary 
front-panel display). Messages to other TID values are rejected with ACK10 = 2. 
 
TIACK 
Format:  B[1] 
Time Set Acknowledge Code. Returned in S2F32 after an S2F31 Date and Time Set request. 
Value Meaning 
0 Accepted — clock updated successfully 
1 Not accepted — format error (TIME string does not match TimeFormat) 
 
 
TIME 
Format:  A[16] 
Date and Time. 16-character ASCII timestamp in format YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc: year (4), month (2), day (2), hour (2), 
minute (2), second (2), centisecond (2). This is the format defined in SEMI E5 and governed by the TimeFormat 
Equipment Constant (Section 2.16). All digits are zero-padded. 
 
TOTSMP 
Format:  U4 
Total Samples. The total number of trace samples to collect before the trace automatically stops. A value of 0 in S2F23 
with a valid TRID stops and deletes an existing trace. Sent in S2F23. 
 
TRID 
Format:  U4 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
Trace ID. A user-assigned 32-bit unsigned integer identifying a Time-Driven Trace. Must be unique among active traces. 
Used in S2F23 (Trace Initialize), S6F1 (Trace Data Send). 
 
UNITS 
Format:  A[n] 
Engineering Units. ASCII string expressing the measurement units of a Status Variable, Data Variable, or Equipment 
Constant. Unit strings follow the notation defined in Chapter 6 (E5 and E145 Units and Symbols). An empty UNITS string 
indicates a dimensionless quantity. 
 
UPPERDB 
Format:  F4 
Upper Deadband. The upper alarm limit boundary in variable engineering units. When a monitored variable value exceeds 
UPPERDB, the equipment transitions to UPPERALARM state and generates CEID 600 (LimitZoneChange). Sent in 
S2F45. 
 
UPPERZONE 
Format:  F4 
Upper Zone Boundary. The upper warning limit boundary in variable engineering units. When a monitored variable value 
exceeds UPPERZONE (but remains below UPPERDB), the equipment transitions to UPPERWARNING state. Sent in 
S2F45. 
 
VID 
Format:  U4 
Variable ID. A generic 32-bit unsigned integer referencing either an SVID (Status Variable ID) or DVID (Data Variable ID) 
in contexts where both types may be used. Used in S2F33 (Define Report VID list), S2F35 (Link Event Report VID 
association), and S1F21/S1F22 (Data Variable Namelist).

5   Variable Item Dictionary 
This chapter provides complete dictionary entries for all Status Variables (SVIDs), Collection Events (CEIDs), 
and Equipment Constants (ECIDs) defined on the Shellback 200mm. Items are organized by type and listed 
in numeric order within each category. 
 
Status Variables reflect real-time equipment state and are retrieved using S1F3/S1F4. Equipment Constants 
are configuration parameters that may be read with S2F13/S2F14 and modified with S2F15/S2F16. Collection 
Events represent significant equipment occurrences reported to the host via S6F11. 
 
5.1   Status Variables 
All Status Variables may be included in host-defined Event Reports (S2F33/S2F35) and Time-Driven Traces 
(S2F23). Status Variables marked as process-related are updated in real time during recipe execution.

5.2   Collection Events 
The following Collection Events are defined on the Shellback 200mm. All events may be enabled or disabled 
individually using S2F37/S2F38. The default state for all events at power-on is determined by the 
DefaultCEIDState Equipment Constant (ECID 1031). The SVIDs shown in the "Default Variables" column are 
those included in the predefined report links described in Section 2.8.1; host -defined reports may reference 
any SVID.

5.3   Equipment Constants 
Equipment Constants are persistent configuration parameters stored on the equipment controller. Changes 
made via S2F15 take effect immediately unless otherwise noted and survive equipment power cycles. Min 
and Max columns specify the allowable range for numeric constants; entries marked "—" do not have a 
numeric range constraint.

6   E5 and E145 Units and Symbols 
This chapter lists the engineering units and symbols used in UNITS strings throughout this document, in 
conformance with SEMI E5-0219 (SECS-II) and SEMI E145-0712 (Units and Symbols for Semiconductor 
Manufacturing Equipment). 
 
UNITS strings appear in S1F12 (Status Variable Namelist), S2F30 (Equipment Constant Namelist), and 
related namelist reply messages. They provide the host with the measurement units for each variable, 
enabling correct engineering interpretation of numeric values. Units are expressed as ASCII strings; 
compound units are formed using the standard SEMI E145 notation.  
 
Pressure 
Symbol Unit Name Usage in This Document 
mTorr Millitorr Process chamber vacuum pressure (primary unit) 
Torr Torr Higher-range vacuum pressure 
Pa Pascal SI unit of pressure (1 Torr = 133.322 Pa) 
atm Atmosphere Atmospheric reference pressure (1 atm = 760 Torr) 
 
Temperature 
Symbol Unit Name Usage in This Document 
°C Degree Celsius Chamber temperature, setpoint temperature 
K Kelvin Absolute temperature (used in some derived process 
parameters) 
 
Power 
Symbol Unit Name Usage in This Document 
W Watt RF generator forward and reflected power 
kW Kilowatt High-power process parameters 
kWh Kilowatt-hour Accumulated target energy (lifetime tracking) 
 
Voltage 
Symbol Unit Name Usage in This Document 
V Volt Target bias voltage, process electrode potential 
kV Kilovolt High-voltage supply diagnostics

© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page

6.1   Compound Unit Notation 
Compound units are formed according to SEMI E145 notation rules. Multiplication is indicated by a middle dot 
(·) or by juxtaposition; division is indicated by a forward slash (/). 
 
Symbol Meaning Example 
nm/s Nanometre per second DepositionRate (SVID 95) 
sccm Standard cm³ per minute ArgonFlowRate (SVID 97) — note: sccm 
is a single token 
kWh Kilowatt-hour TargetLifetime (SVID 98) 
°C Degree Celsius ChamberTemperature (SVID 91) 
 
6.2   Standard Condition Definitions 
For gas flow measurements expressed in sccm or slm, standard conditions are defined as 0 °C (273.15 K) 
and 101.325 kPa (1 atm), per SEMI E145. Mass flow controllers on the Shellback 200mm are calibrated to 
these reference conditions for Argon (Ar) gas unless otherwise specified on the equipment configuration 
record. 
 
For pressure measurements, the Shellback 200mm reports absolute pressure. All chamber pressure readings 
(SVID 90) represent total gas load pressure, not gauge pressure. 
 
6.3   Conversion Factors 
 
From To Conversion Factor 
Torr Pa 1 Torr = 133.322 Pa 
Shellback 200mm Host Interface Guide Revision 3.2  |  CONFIDENTIAL 
© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page  
From To Conversion Factor 
Torr mTorr 1 Torr = 1000 mTorr 
Å nm 1 Å = 0.1 nm 
Å/s nm/s 1 Å/s = 0.1 nm/s 
°C K T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15 
kWh MJ 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ

1 Introduction 
 
1.1 Equipment Description 
The Shellback 200mm is a single-wafer processing system designed for use in semiconductor manufacturing 
environments. The equipment is capable of performing physical vapor deposition (PVD) operations on 
200mm silicon wafers. It is equipped with a multi-chamber architecture consisting of a transfer module, load 
lock chambers, and process chambers. 
The equipment is controlled by an embedded host controller running a real-time operating system. 
Communication with the fab host is established via the SECS/GEM protocol suite as defined in the applicable 
SEMI standards. This document describes the host interface as implemented on the Shellback 200mm 
platform. 
 
1.2 Equipment Operations 
The Shellback 200mm supports the following primary operational functions:hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$5c5c4e49-415b-4a7d-9a69-0b145d4ead47h
)}(h
}(hhöh}(hKhhhhhhhhhKhKuhXò␀␀platform. 
 
1.2 Equipment Operations 
The Shellback 200mm supports the following primary operational functions: 
â¢ Wafer loading and unloading via FOUP (Front Opening Unified Pod) interface 
â¢ Automated wafer transfer between load lock and process chambers 
â¢ Process recipe execution and management 
â¢ Real-time process parameter monitoring and data collection 
â¢ Alarm detection, notification, and response 
â¢ Remote command execution initiated by the MES host 
â¢ Spooled message delivery during communication interruptions 
 
All operations are subject to the equipment control states as defined in Section 2.2. The equipment will only 
accept process commands when in the appropriate control state as defined by the GEM standard (SEMI 
E30). 
 
1.3 Human Machine Interface 
The Shellback 200mm is equipped with an operator terminal (HMI) that provides local control capability. The 
HMI is a touch-screen panel mounted on the front of the equipment. The HMI provides the following functions:hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$1e0ca0ab-e78e-466f-98cd-b17fbe3fa3e9h
)}(h
}(hhýh}(hKhhhhhhhhhKhK uhXÏ␀␀HMI is a touch-screen panel mounted on the front of the equipment. The HMI provides the following functions: 
â¢ Display of current equipment state, active alarms, and process status 
â¢ Local initiation of equipment control state transitions 
â¢ Recipe selection and initiation in local mode 
â¢ Access to maintenance and diagnostic functions 
â¢ Review of historical alarm and event logs 
 
The HMI operates in parallel with the SECS/GEM host interface. The operator can transfer control between 
Local and Remote states as described in Section 2.2. When the equipment is in the Remote state, process 
initiation from the HMI is disabled and control authority rests with the host.

1.6 Host Communication â E37-1018 HSMS 
The primary communication method between the Shellback 200mm and the host is HSMS (High Speed 
Message Services) as defined in SEMI E37 and E37.1 (Single Session Mode). HSMS uses TCP/IP as the 
underlying transport protocol, providing a reliable, connection-oriented communication channel. 
 
1.6.1 Physical Connector 
The equipment provides a standard RJ-45 Ethernet connector for host communication. The connector is 
located on the rear panel of the equipment controller cabinet and is labeled "HOST". The electrical 
characteristics comply with IEEE 802.3 (Ethernet) 100BASE-TX. A shielded Cat5e or Cat6 cable should be 
used for the connection.

1.7 SECS-II Messaging - SEMI E5-0219 
All application-level messages exchanged between the Shellback 200mm and the host are formatted 
according to SECS-II (SEMI E5). Each SECS-II message is identified by a Stream number and a Function 
number (SxFy notation). The equipment supports both primary messages (odd function numbers, sent by 
either equipment or host) and secondary messages (even function numbers, which are reply messages). 
SECS-II data items are encoded using the SECS-II item format codes as defined in SEMI E5. The data types 
used in this document are listed in the Data Item Dictionary (Chapter 4).

2 GEM Capabilities 
 
This chapter describes the GEM capabilities as implemented on the Shellback 200mm. Each section follows 
the standard GEM capability description format, covering: Configuration Options, Variables, Events, and 
Scenarios where applicable. 
 
2.1 Establish Communications 
The Establish Communications capability defines the procedures by which the equipment and host initiate 
and maintain a SECS/GEM communication session. This includes the state machine governing the 
communication session, the variables associated with communication state, and the scenarios for session 
establishment and loss. 
 
2.1.1 Communications States & Transitions 
The equipment implements the GEM Communications State Model. The state machine has two top -level 
states: DISABLED and ENABLED. The ENABLED state contains two sub-states: NOT COMMUNICATING 
and COMMUNICATING.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$a5c4ffa5-1b2c-420a-8000-72e6aafa7330h
)}(h
}(hjQ␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK
hK,uhXÇ␀␀states: DISABLED and ENABLED. The ENABLED state contains two sub-states: NOT COMMUNICATING 
and COMMUNICATING. 
 
DISABLED State: 
In the DISABLED state, the equipment will not send or receive any SECS messages. This state is entered at 
power-on and is exited by operator action via the HMI or upon receiving the Enable command. 
 
NOT COMMUNICATING Sub-state: 
In the NOT COMMUNICATING sub-state, the HSMS transport layer may or may not be connected. The 
equipment sends S1F13 (Establish Communications Request) to the host upon entering this state. Transition 
to COMMUNICATING occurs upon receiving a valid S1F14 response from the host. 
 
COMMUNICATING Sub-state: 
In the COMMUNICATING sub-state, all GEM messaging is active. The equipment sends collection events, 
processes remote commands, and responds to host requests. Loss of communications (T3 timeout, TCP 
disconnect) causes a transition back to NOT COMMUNICATING. 
 
Trans. From State To State Triggerhh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$21829278-e4d9-4025-adcf-54e98d29a8f8h
)}(h
}(hjX␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK
hK-uhX/␀␀processes remote commands, and responds to host requests. Loss of communications (T3 timeout, TCP 
disconnect) causes a transition back to NOT COMMUNICATING.

2.2 Control 
The Control capability defines the states and transitions governing the level of host control authority over the 
equipment. Control state directly affects whether the equipment accepts remote commands and process 
initiation from the host or from the local operator. 
 
2.2.1 Control States & Transitions 
The Shellback 200mm implements the standard GEM Control State Model. The primary states are 
EQUIPMENT OFFLINE, ATTEMPT ONLINE, and ONLINE. The ONLINE state contains sub -states: HOST 
OFFLINE, LOCAL, and REMOTE. 
 
Trans. From State To State Trigger / Condition 
T1 EQUIPMENT OFFLINE ATTEMPT ONLINE Operator selects "Go Online" from HMI 
T2 ATTEMPT ONLINE HOST OFFLINE Host does not send S1F17 within 
timeout

2.7 Event Notification 
The Event Notification capability provides the mechanism by which the equipment proactively reports 
significant occurrences to the host. The equipment supports the Collection Event model defined in SEMI E30. 
Collection Events are identified by a Collection Event ID (CEID) and reported to the host via S6F11 (Event 
Report Send), to which the host replies with S6F12 (Event Report Acknowledge). The host may enable or 
disable individual Collection Events using S2F37 (Enable/Disable Event Report), acknowledged by S2F38.

2.10 Equipment Constants 
Equipment Constants (ECs) are configuration parameters that govern equipment behavior and may be read 
or modified by the host. ECs are identified by Equipment Constant ID (ECID) and are persisted across power 
cycles. The host reads ECs using S2F13 (Equipment Constant Request) / S2F14 (Equipment Constant Data), 
and writes ECs using S2F15 (New Equipment Constant Send) / S2F16 (New Equipment Constant 
Acknowledge). 
2.10.1 Configuration Options

FALSE, all ECs are read-only to the host. 
ECChangeLogDepth 100 Number of Equipment Constant change events retained in the 
equipment's audit log.

2.13 Alarm Management

2.17 Error Messages 
The Shellback 200mm uses SECS Stream 9 to report message-level errors to the host. Stream 9 messages 
are sent by the equipment in response to host messages that cannot be processed due to format errors, 
unrecognized message identifiers, or message sequencing violations. Stream 9 messages are primary 
messages sent without reply and are used solely to notify the host of a communication -level problem; they do 
not affect equipment process state.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$27843bfc-0365-4e91-8ea1-bbb99ad06118h
)}(h

Â© 2024 Fab Equipment Systems. All rights reserved. Page 
The equipment does not send a Stream 9 message for application-level errors (for example, a rejected 
Remote Command). Those errors are reported through the appropriate reply message (e.g., HCACK in 
S2F42).

2.18 Limits Monitoring 
Limits Monitoring allows the host to define upper and lower threshold values for selected Status Variables. 
When a variable's value crosses a defined limit, the equipment generates a Limits Monitoring event. Limits 
may be configured to define an inner zone (warning) and an outer zone (alarm) around a nominal value. This 
capability is defined in SEMI E30 as an Additional Capability. 
Limits are configured using S2F45 (Define Variable Limit Attributes) / S2F46 (Variable Limit Attribute 
Acknowledge), and queried using S2F47 (Variable Limit Attribute Request) / S2F48 (Variable Limit Attribute 
Data). Each limit definition includes an upper limit (UPPERDB), a lower limit (LOWERDB), an upper zone

2.19 Spooling 
Spooling provides reliable delivery of SECS messages during periods when the host communication link is 
unavailable. When spooling is enabled and the equipment is in the NOT COMMUNICATING state (Section 
2.1), outgoing primary messages that would otherwise be discarded are stored in a local spool buffer. Upon 
re-establishing communication, the equipment delivers spooled messages to the host in the order they were 
generated. This capability is defined in SEMI E30 as an Additional Capability. 
Spooling applies to equipment-originated primary messages only: principally collection event reports (S6F11) 
and alarm notifications (S5F1). The host activates and deactivates spooling using S2F43 (Reset Spooling 
Streams and Functions) / S2F44 (Reset Spooling Acknowledge). The equipment acknowledges spooledhh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$891982a5-7974-433c-a83a-938b558ff00bh
)}(h
}(hjÒ␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK!hKcuhX␀␀Streams and Functions) / S2F44 (Reset Spooling Acknowledge). The equipment acknowledges spooled 
message delivery using S6F24 (Spool Transmit Acknowledge). 
2.19.1 Spooling Sequence 
The spooling operational sequence is as follows: 
â¢ Host activates spooling for the desired streams and functions using S2F43. 
â¢ While the equipment is in the COMMUNICATING state, messages are delivered normally without 
spooling. 
â¢ When communication is lost (transition to NOT COMMUNICATING), the equipment begins spooling 
qualifying outgoing primary messages to the local spool buffer. 
â¢ When the COMMUNICATING state is re-entered, the equipment notifies the host that a spool exists 
by sending S6F23 (Request Spooled Data) prior to delivering any new live messages. 
â¢ The host requests spool delivery by sending S6F23 (if necessary to initiate) or the equipment sends 
spooled messages beginning from the oldest entry.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$e7171663-a38d-4ff0-8867-1903df377bcbh
)}(h
}(hjÙ␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK!hKduhXÁ␀␀â¢ The host requests spool delivery by sending S6F23 (if necessary to initiate) or the equipment sends 
spooled messages beginning from the oldest entry. 
â¢ Each spooled message is delivered and individually acknowledged by the host (S6F24, ACKC6 = 0). 
â¢ Upon successful delivery of all spooled messages, the spool buffer is cleared.

control state machines.

3.8 Stream 9: System Errors 
Stream 9 messages are sent by the equipment to report protocol-level errors to the host. These messages 
are primary messages sent without reply (W-bit not set). They do not affect equipment process state and 
serve only as diagnostic notifications. 
Message Name Trigger 
S9F1 Unrecognized Device ID Message received with an unrecognized Device ID. 
S9F3 Unrecognized Stream Type Message received with an unsupported Stream number. 
S9F5 Unrecognized Function Type Supported Stream but unsupported Function number received. 
S9F7 Illegal Data Recognized SxFy received but with a malformed data structure. 
S9F9 Transaction Timer Timeout Equipment sent a W-bit primary message and did not receive a 
reply within T3. 
S9F11 Data Too Long Received message body exceeds the maximum allowed block 
size.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$14ebef5f-a7dc-48de-a640-7da8abe0add8h
)}(h
}(hj␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK5hKuhXÑ␀␀S9F9 Transaction Timer Timeout Equipment sent a W-bit primary message and did not receive a 
reply within T3. 
S9F11 Data Too Long Received message body exceeds the maximum allowed block 
size. 
S9F13 Conversation Timeout Multi-block conversation did not complete within T4 (if 
applicable). 
 
Each S9 message carries a message header block as the body, providing enough context for the host to 
identify the offending transaction. S9F9 includes the system bytes of the timed -out transaction. No reply is 
expected from the host for any Stream 9 message.

4 Data Item Dictionary 
This chapter defines all SECS-II data items used in the Shellback 200mm host interface. Data items are 
atomic pieces of information transferred within SECS-II messages. Each item is identified by a symbolic name 
and has a defined format code that specifies its data type and encoding as defined in SEMI E5. Data items 
appear as leaf nodes in the nested List structures of SECS-II message bodies. 
 
Data items are listed alphabetically. Where an item carries a defined set of enumerated values, the valid 
values and their meanings are described. For items whose values are equipment -specific (such as variable 
IDs and event IDs), the values are defined in this document's respective section or in the Variable Item 
Dictionary (Chapter 5).

Dictionary (Chapter 5).

5 Variable Item Dictionary 
This chapter provides complete dictionary entries for all Status Variables (SVIDs), Collection Events (CEIDs), 
and Equipment Constants (ECIDs) defined on the Shellback 200mm. Items are organized by type and listed 
in numeric order within each category. 
 
Status Variables reflect real-time equipment state and are retrieved using S1F3/S1F4. Equipment Constants 
are configuration parameters that may be read with S2F13/S2F14 and modified with S2F15/S2F16. Collection 
Events represent significant equipment occurrences reported to the host via S6F11. 
 
5.1 Status Variables 
All Status Variables may be included in host-defined Event Reports (S2F33/S2F35) and Time-Driven Traces 
(S2F23). Status Variables marked as process-related are updated in real time during recipe execution.

6 E5 and E145 Units and Symbols 
This chapter lists the engineering units and symbols used in UNITS strings throughout this document, in 
conformance with SEMI E5-0219 (SECS-II) and SEMI E145-0712 (Units and Symbols for Semiconductor 
Manufacturing Equipment). 
 
UNITS strings appear in S1F12 (Status Variable Namelist), S2F30 (Equipment Constant Namelist), and 
related namelist reply messages. They provide the host with the measurement units for each variable, 
enabling correct engineering interpretation of numeric values. Units are expressed as ASCII strings; 
compound units are formed using the standard SEMI E145 notation.

6.2 Standard Condition Definitions 
For gas flow measurements expressed in sccm or slm, standard conditions are defined as 0 Â°C (273.15 K) 
and 101.325 kPa (1 atm), per SEMI E145. Mass flow controllers on the Shellback 200mm are calibrated to 
these reference conditions for Argon (Ar) gas unless otherwise specified on the equipment configuration 
record. 
 
For pressure measurements, the Shellback 200mm reports absolute pressure. All chamber pressure readings 
(SVID 90) represent total gas load pressure, not gauge pressure.

Chapter 1 — Introduction
1.1 Purpose and Scope
This document defines the SECS/GEM host-to-equipment interface for the CVD-F800 Dual-Chamber Thermal
Chemical Vapor Deposition system. It specifies all Status Variables (SV), Data Variables (DV), Collection Events
(CEID), Alarms, Remote Commands (RCMD), Reports (RPTID), and state machine transitions required for full GEM
compliance under SEMI E30. Host systems integrating this equipment shall use this document as the authoritative
reference for all message exchanges, variable polling, event subscriptions, and alarm management.
1.2 GEM Compliance Summary
The CVD-F800 implements the complete set of required and selected optional GEM capabilities as listed below. All
SEMI E30 mandatory capabilities are implemented.

Chapter 2 — Equipment Configuration
2.1 Physical and Electrical Setup
The CVD-F800 connects to the host factory network via a dedicated 1 Gbps Ethernet interface. The equipment
controller runs an embedded Linux OS and exposes the SECS/GEM interface through a single HSMS-SS passive
listener. All communication is on VLAN 30 (Equipment Network). A separate service port (VLAN 50) is reserved for
maintenance and is not part of the GEM interface.

3.2 Dual-Chamber Architecture
The CVD-F800 employs two independently controlled process chambers sharing a common wafer handling robot and
gas delivery manifold. Each chamber has its own temperature controller (5-zone heater stack), pressure controller, RF
generator, and gas injection ring. Chambers may run different recipes simultaneously. The shared robot services both
chambers and reports its status through the global SV range (VID 1000–1099). Chamber-specific interlocks ensure
that a fault in Chamber A does not abort an active process in Chamber B unless a shared resource (gas manifold,
exhaust) is affected.

CVD-F800 SECS/GEM Interface Specification  |  Revision C  |  FabTech Systems Inc.
Page 8
Chapter 4 — Status Variables (SV)
Status Variables are real-time equipment parameters that the host may read at any time using S1F3/F4 (request
selected equipment status) or S1F5/F6 (request formatted status). All SVIDs are read-only unless noted otherwise.
Values are refreshed by the equipment controller at the update rates shown.

Chapter 5 — Data Variables (DV)
Data Variables represent process parameters, recipe settings, and metrology results. They are typically read after a
process event (e.g., at ProcessEnd) using S6F1/F2 or as part of a linked report delivered with S6F11. Unlike Status
Variables, DVs may have undefined values outside of an active process step.

Chapter 6 — Collection Events (CEID)
Collection Events are named points in the equipment's process or control flow at which the equipment notifies the host
and delivers a set of associated variable values. Events are reported via S6F11 (Event Report Send). The host
enables event reporting using S2F37 (Enable/Disable Event Report).

Chapter 7 — Reports (RPTID)
Reports define named collections of variables that are delivered to the host when a linked Collection Event fires. The
host configures report-event links using S2F33 (Define Report) and S2F35 (Link Event Report). Default links are
established at equipment startup and persist until the host redefines them.

Chapter 8 — Alarm Definitions
Alarms are abnormal equipment conditions reported to the host via S5F1 (Alarm Report Send). Critical alarms result in
immediate process abort. Warning alarms are logged and reported but do not abort the process unless the condition
persists beyond the defined tolerance window. All alarms may be individually enabled or disabled by the host using
S5F3.
8.1 Critical Alarms (Severity: CRITICAL)

 ID
 Name
 Code
 Linked SVID
 Description

 Any Chamber A heater zone exceeds 1200 degC
 (hard limit)

Chapter 9 — Remote Commands (RCMD)
Remote Commands allow the host to initiate equipment actions using S2F41 (Host Command Send). The equipment
acknowledges each command with S2F42. Commands that affect process state will generate corresponding
Collection Events upon completion. Parameters are passed as a list of CPNAME/CPVAL pairs in the S2F41 body.

Chapter 10 — Equipment State Machine
10.1 State Definitions
Each process chamber maintains an independent sub-state. The global equipment state is the composite of both
chambers. The GEM Control State (SV 1002) is a separate orthogonal state machine defined by SEMI E30.
 State
 Applies To
 Description
IDLE
 Chamber A/B
 Chamber is at atmospheric pressure, at ambient temperature, and ready to
 accept a new process request.
PUMPING
 Chamber A/B
 Vacuum pump-down in progress. Pressure is decreasing towards base vacuum.
PURGE
 Chamber A/B
 N2 purge gas flowing. Chamber is being cleaned of residual gases prior to
 process.
RAMP
 Chamber A/B
 Heaters ramping temperature towards the process setpoint at the programmed
 ramp rate.
SOAK
 Chamber A/B
 Temperature within tolerance of setpoint. Waiting for thermal stabilisation period
 to expire.
DEPOSIT
 Chamber A/B
Active deposition step. Process gases flowing, RF on (for PECVD recipes), wafer
 being processed.
COOL
 Chamber A/B
 Heaters off or set to low temperature. Chamber cooling before wafer unload.
VENT
 Chamber A/B
 N2 vent in progress. Pressure rising to atmospheric for safe wafer unload.
COMPLETED
 Chamber A/B
 Process run finished successfully. Wafer ready for unload by robot.
FAULT
 Chamber A/B
 A critical alarm has stopped the process. Chamber not available until fault is
 cleared.
MAINTENANCE
 Global
 Equipment-wide maintenance mode. Both chambers inhibited.
