Appendix C — Alarm Response Procedures (Detailed)
ALID 4001 / 4006 — Chamber Over-Temperature
1. Send ABORT_PROCESS RCMD immediately for the affected chamber.
2. Do NOT open the chamber door. Allow natural cool-down with N2 flowing.
3. Monitor SVIDs 1101–1105 (or 1201–1205) until all zones <200 degC.
4. Check thermocouple continuity on the faulted zone.
5. Inspect heater power relay and zone controller for faults.
6. If hardware confirmed healthy, send RESET_FAULT RCMD with FAULT_CODE=0x01.
7. If fault recurs within 3 cycles, schedule preventive maintenance.
ALID 4003 / 4008 — Plasma Failure
1. Verify process gas flows are within specification (check SVIDs 1301–1308).
2. Check RF generator fault code (accessible via S10 terminal message).
3. Verify chamber pressure is within ignition range (50–500 mTorr).
4. Send START_PROCESS RCMD again (up to 2 automatic retries are allowed).
5. If 3 consecutive ignition failures, lock out the chamber and call RF maintenance.
ALID 4005 / 4010 — Gas Leak Detected
1. Immediately activate facility gas shutoff valve for the affected gas species.
2. Evacuate all personnel from the gas cabinet bay.
3. Notify facility safety officer before re-entry.
4. Do not send RESET_FAULT until leak source is confirmed cleared by leak detection.
5. Document event in facility safety log.
ALID 4013 — EMO Activated
1. Identify the cause of the EMO activation before approaching equipment.
2. All in-progress processes are aborted. Wafers in chambers may be at risk.
3. Follow lockout/tagout procedure before any physical inspection.
4. Once safe, perform full equipment integrity check before resetting EMO.
5. Issue RESET_FAULT after safety check is documented and signed off.

5. Equipment Description and Operations
The ETCH-PRO-X100 is a plasma etching system used for semiconductor wafer processing. It executes recipe-driven
etch sequences in a controlled chamber using vacuum control, process gas delivery, RF power, plasma ignition,
endpoint monitoring, and post-process completion handling. The host interface supports production integration with
MES/CIM systems for data collection, alarms, remote control, recipes, and recovery from communication loss.
5.1 Plasma Etching Purpose
- Remove selected films or material layers from wafer surfaces using plasma chemistry and RF energy.
- Maintain process repeatability by monitoring chamber pressure, gas flow, RF power, temperature, plasma state,
endpoint status, and process duration.
- Generate traceability records at lot, carrier, wafer, recipe, process start, plasma ignition, and process completion
points.
5.2 Wafer Processing Flow
Step
Operation
Host Interface Impact
1
Carrier loaded and material context
identified
CEID 5200 CarrierLoaded can report CarrierID, LotID, WaferID, and status.
2
Recipe/PPID selected or downloaded
S7F3/S7F4 may download process program; ActiveRecipe and RecipeID updated.
3
Host sends START alias or INITIALIZE
S2F41 command accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE with required RecipeID.
4
Setup and chamber preparation
ProcessState moves IDLE -> SETUP; pressure/gas/RF prerequisites checked.
5
Plasma process executes
ProcessState PROCESSING; CEID 5100 PlasmaIgnition; SVs and trace data available.
6
Completion and result calculation
CEID 5002 ProcessCompleted; ProcessCompletionReport includes completion DVs.
7
Carrier unload or next wafer
CEID 5201 CarrierUnloaded or next wafer sequence.
5.3 Host/MES Interface Purpose
- Establish a reliable SECS/GEM HSMS link for production automation.
- Provide status, trace, and event data for equipment and process characterization.
- Support alarms with S5F1/S5F2 set/clear notification and alarm list retrieval.
- Permit controlled remote operation via S2F41/S2F42 when in ON-LINE REMOTE.
- Manage process programs using S7 download/upload transactions.
- Spool alarm and event messages during communication loss and deliver them after recovery.

6. SEMI Standards Supported
The ETCH-PRO-X100 host interface follows the SECS/GEM standards family. The system uses HSMS over TCP/IP as
the transport and SECS-II/GEM for application-level messages. SECS-I is referenced for historical SECS definitions but
is not the active physical communication path for this equipment.
Standard

Description

ETCH-PRO-X100 uses HSMS, not serial SECS-I.

SECS-II message content, stream/function definitions, and data item encoding.
SEMI E30

High-Speed Message Services (HSMS) over TCP/IP.

SEMI E145

Protocol statement: ETCH-PRO-X100 supports SECS/GEM over HSMS single-session operation. The implemented host
interface is documented as Rev A for this equipment manual.

7. HSMS Connection Settings
The ETCH-PRO-X100 operates in HSMS Passive mode. The equipment listens on TCP port 5011, and the fab host
initiates the connection. Device ID is 0 for the single logical device.

8.1 Compliance Summary
The ETCH-PRO-X100 implements the required host communication, state model, data collection, alarm, control,
clock, and remote command functions needed for a production SECS/GEM integration. Additional functions such as
trace data, dynamic event report configuration, limits monitoring, process program management, equipment
terminal services, and spooling are documented for characterization and host qualification.
8.2 Overall GEM Compliance Status
Overall GEM Compliance Status: Supported for the documented ETCH-PRO-X100 Rev A interface. Some capabilities, such as
material movement, are limited to carrier/wafer event reporting and do not claim complete SEMI E87 carrier management.

9.1 PPID and PPBODY Handling
The process program identifier (PPID) is represented by RecipeID / ActiveRecipe and is used to select the etch
process recipe. PPBODY is supported as an unformatted body through S7F3 process program download and
S7F5/S7F6 process program upload. The equipment validates the PPID, required recipe structure, chamber limits,
gas/RF setpoints, maximum process time, and endpoint configuration before accepting process execution.
Function
Message Pair
Behavior
Download recipe
S7F3/S7F4
Host sends PPID and PPBODY. ACKC7=0 indicates accepted.
Upload recipe
S7F5/S7F6
Host requests PPID; equipment returns PPBODY if stored.
Delete recipe
S7F17/S7F18
Host requests deletion; equipment rejects active recipe deletion.
Directory request
S7F19/S7F20
Equipment returns current process program directory.

10E. Process State Reference
State ID
State Name
Description
PROC-0
IDLE
Initial process state. Equipment is not processing, no active wafer in etch sequence, and START/INITIALIZE
may be accepted if in REMOTE.
PROC-1
SETUP
Recipe and material context are being validated; chamber preparation may start.
PROC-2
PROCESSING
Wafer etch is active; plasma, gas flow, RF power, pressure, and endpoint are monitored.
PROC-3
PAUSED
Processing is temporarily suspended by PAUSE or an interlock condition that permits resume.
PROC-4
COMPLETING
Etch sequence is ending, post-process purge/vent/robot handoff and result calculation are underway.
PROC-5
ERROR
Fault state caused by critical alarm, failed command, unsafe pressure/temperature, or unrecoverable
transfer error.
10F. Process State Transitions
Transition
From State
To State
Trigger / Condition
P-T1
IDLE
SETUP

P-T2

PROCESSING

begins.
P-T3
PROCESSING
COMPLETING

P-T4
COMPLETING
IDLE
Post-process clean-up complete and CEID 5002 ProcessCompleted emitted.
P-T5
PROCESSING
PAUSED

P-T6
PAUSED
PROCESSING

P-T7
PROCESSING
ERROR
Critical alarm such as ChamberOverheat, VacuumPressureTooHigh, RFPowerFault,
DoorInterlockOpen, EmergencyStopActivated, or WaferTransferError occurs.
P-T8
ERROR
IDLE
Fault cleared and host/operator sends RESET; reset accepted only after physical
alarm condition is resolved.

14. Alarm Verification
The ETCH-PRO-X100 defines ALID 1001-1015. All alarms are reported using S5F1 when enabled. The ALCD alarm
code uses bit 7 to indicate set/clear: bit 7 set indicates alarm SET; bit 7 clear indicates alarm CLEAR.
Alarm ID
Alarm Code
Alarm Name
Severity
Description
1001
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
ChamberOverheat
Critical
Chamber temperature exceeded maximum safe limit.
1002
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
RobotNotHomed
Warning
Wafer transfer robot has not returned to home position.
1003
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
VacuumPressureTooHigh
Critical
Chamber vacuum pressure exceeded maximum allowed value.
1004
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
VacuumPumpFailure
Warning
Vacuum pump failed, degraded, or did not reach expected vacuum
condition.
1005
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
GasFlowOutOfRange
Warning
Measured process gas flow is outside configured tolerance.
1006
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
RFPowerFault
Critical
RF generator, match network, or forward/reflected RF power fault
detected during processing.
1007
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
CoolingWaterTempHigh
Warning
Cooling water temperature exceeded configured limit.
1008
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
CoolingWaterFlowLow
Warning
Cooling water flow rate is below minimum safe operating flow.
1009
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
DoorInterlockOpen
Critical
Equipment door interlock opened during operation.
1010
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Critical
Emergency stop button was activated.

CLEAR

0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Warning

0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Wafer transfer robot or sensor detected transfer error.
1014
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
SystemCommunicationTimeout
Warning
Internal or host communication timeout detected.
1015
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
MaintenanceDue
Warning
Scheduled maintenance interval reached.
Mass filter / beam drift applicability: No ALID is assigned to MassFilterFault. No ALID is assigned to BeamDrift. These
conditions are not applicable to ETCH-PRO-X100 unless explicitly documented by a future equipment revision. Closest
related ETCH-PRO alarms are GasFlowOutOfRange (ALID 1005) and RFPowerFault (ALID 1006).
14.1 Alarm Recovery Procedures
Alarm / Condition
Equipment Action
Host Recovery Action
ChamberOverheat (1001)
Immediate process halt, RF off, transition to ERROR.
Acknowledge S5F1, investigate temperature root cause, wait for
clear, send RESET.
VacuumPressureTooHigh (1003)
Immediate process halt or safe stop, transition to ERROR.
Acknowledge, verify vacuum/pump state, clear physical
condition, send RESET.
RFPowerFault (1006)
RF output disabled; process abort may be required.
Acknowledge, verify generator/match network, restart only after
RESET or safe idle.
DoorInterlockOpen (1009)
Process inhibited or halted; safety interlock enforced.
Acknowledge and keep equipment blocked until door interlock is
restored.
EmergencyStopActivated (1010)
All motion/process activity stopped; ERROR state.
Acknowledge, require operator reset at tool, then send RESET
only after E-stop release.
WaferTransferError (1013)
Robot/wafer transfer stops; wafer status requires operator
verification.
Acknowledge, resolve transfer condition, verify wafer location,
send RESET if permitted.
Warning alarms
(1002,1004,1005,1007,1008,1011,1012,1014,1015)
Process may continue or pause depending on recipe/site
policy.
Acknowledge, log, and decide whether to STOP, allow
continuation, or schedule maintenance.

16. Remote Commands
START inconsistency resolved: START is documented as the host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Hosts may
send RCMD="START"; the equipment executes the INITIALIZE process-start path and reports command history as START
while mapping execution to INITIALIZE internally.
Command Name
Description
Parameters
START
Host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Starts process setup and
processing when accepted.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
INITIALIZE
Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
STOP
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
PAUSE
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
Optional: ReasonCode.
RESUME
Resumes process from PAUSED state after conditions are valid.
No required parameters. Optional: ReasonCode.
RESET
Clears ERROR state after alarms are resolved and returns process state to
IDLE.
Optional: ResetMode, ReasonCode.
PUMP_DOWN
Starts chamber pump-down sequence when idle and interlocks are safe.
Optional: ChamberID, TargetPressure.
VENT
Starts chamber vent sequence when idle or maintenance mode allows.
Optional: ChamberID, VentMode.
CLEAN_CHAMBER
Runs chamber clean recipe or predefined clean cycle.
Required: RecipeID or CleanRecipeID. Optional: ChamberID.
16.1 START Parameter Requirements
Item
Requirement
Required parameters
RecipeID
Optional parameters
LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID
Allowed state
Control state must be ON-LINE REMOTE and process state must be IDLE
Success behavior
S2F42 HCACK=0; emits CEID 5001 ProcessStarted and later CEID 5002 ProcessCompleted
Invalid parameter behavior
S2F42 parameter error; command rejected and no process state transition occurs
START alias rule
START is accepted as host-facing alias for INITIALIZE; INITIALIZE remains the canonical equipment command

16.4 S2F42 Acknowledgement and Parameter Validation
Code / Field
Meaning
Typical Cause / Host Action
HCACK=0
Command accepted
Command will execute or has been queued. Monitor LastCommandStatus and CEIDs.
HCACK=1
Command does not exist
RCMD spelling mismatch or unsupported command. Use START, INITIALIZE, STOP,
PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER.
HCACK=2
Cannot perform now
Wrong process state, unresolved alarm, chamber not safe, or command conflict.
HCACK=3
At least one parameter invalid
CPNAME/CPVAL value is out of range, unsupported, or invalid type.
HCACK=4
Command will be performed with completion
signaled later
Used only if asynchronous command completion is site-configured.
HCACK=5
Rejected, already in desired condition
Example: RESUME when not PAUSED or RESET when already IDLE.
HCACK=6
Rejected in current control state
Equipment is not ON-LINE REMOTE. Request REMOTE/local authorization before retry.
Parameter error
S2F42 command parameter error list returned
Missing required RecipeID for START/INITIALIZE or invalid
ChamberID/CarrierID/WaferID.

17H. Remote Commands Dictionary
Command
Parameters
Description
START
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
Host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Starts process setup and
processing when accepted.
INITIALIZE
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
STOP
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
PAUSE
Optional: ReasonCode.
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
RESUME
No required parameters. Optional: ReasonCode.
Resumes process from PAUSED state after conditions are valid.
RESET
Optional: ResetMode, ReasonCode.
Clears ERROR state after alarms are resolved and returns process state to
IDLE.
PUMP_DOWN
Optional: ChamberID, TargetPressure.
Starts chamber pump-down sequence when idle and interlocks are safe.
VENT
Optional: ChamberID, VentMode.
Starts chamber vent sequence when idle or maintenance mode allows.
CLEAN_CHAMBER
Required: RecipeID or CleanRecipeID. Optional: ChamberID.
Runs chamber clean recipe or predefined clean cycle.

19. Operational Scenarios
The scenarios below summarize the expected sequence and behavior for the most common ETCH-PRO-X100 host
integration tests.
Scenario
Expected Sequence / Result
Establish Communications
Host opens TCP connection to port 5011; HSMS Select succeeds; S1F13/S1F14 returns COMMACK=0; state becomes SELECTED /
COMMUNICATING.
Host synchronizes status
Host sends S1F3/S1F4 for current state, S2F33/S2F35/S2F37 to define/link/enable reports, and S5F3 to enable alarms.
Define/link/enable reports
Host defines RPTID 7004, links it to CEID 5002, and enables CEIDs 5001 and 5002.
Start lot/process
Host sends S2F41 START with RecipeID. START maps to INITIALIZE; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE.
Process completion
Equipment sends S6F11 CEID 5002 with ProcessCompletionReport; host replies S6F12 ACKC6=0.
Alarm set/clear
Equipment sends S5F1 with ALCD bit 7 set for SET and clear for CLEAR; host replies S5F2.
Remote command failure
Missing RecipeID, LOCAL control, non-IDLE process state, or unresolved alarm returns S2F42 nonzero HCACK/parameter error.
Spooling during communication loss
On TCP disconnect or timeout, spooling activates for configured streams/functions. Stored S5F1/S6F11 messages are delivered
after recovery using S6F23/S6F24.
Recovery from ERROR state
Host acknowledges alarm, waits for physical fault clear, sends RESET, and confirms ProcessState returns ERROR -> IDLE.

20.1 Required Question Answer Coverage
The following matrix confirms that the revised ETCH-PRO-X100 manual answers the 15 required extraction
questions.
Question
Answer / Manual Location
1. Tool type or model
Plasma Etching System, Model ETCH-PRO-X100, Tool ID EQP-5000. See Sections 1 and 4.
2. Protocol version
SECS/GEM over HSMS/HSMS-SS using SEMI E5, E30, E37, and E37.1; document Rev A. See Sections 1, 6, and 7.
3. Status variables for monitoring
Yes. SVs include ChamberPressure, ChamberTemperature, RFForwardPower, RFReflectedPower, GasFlowRate,
PlasmaState, EndpointStatus, and state variables. See Section 12.1.
4. Primary DVs related to processing
RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec, ProcessEndStatus,
RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage, EndpointResult. See
Section 12.2.
5. Critical CEIDs during lot start/end
5001 ProcessStarted and 5002 ProcessCompleted; carrier context uses 5200 CarrierLoaded and 5201
CarrierUnloaded. See Section 13.
6. Safety/fault alarms
ALIDs 1001-1015 include ChamberOverheat, VacuumPressureTooHigh, RFPowerFault, DoorInterlockOpen,
EmergencyStopActivated, WaferTransferError, and others. See Section 14.
7. Remote commands
START, INITIALIZE, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER. START is alias for
INITIALIZE. See Section 16.
8. States/transitions
Communication, control, and process state reference/transition tables are included. See Section 10.
9. Default communication state on power-up
NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is
OFF-LINE; process state is IDLE. See Section 10.
10. Process state machine
IDLE -> SETUP -> PROCESSING -> COMPLETING -> IDLE; PROCESSING -> PAUSED -> PROCESSING; PROCESSING ->
ERROR -> IDLE. See Section 10.
11. Spooling support/configuration
Spooling is supported; default enabled, buffer size 5000 messages, retention 24 hr, default streams/functions
include S5F1 and S6F11. See Section 11 and SML in Section 18.
12. Predefined reports
CommunicationStateReport, ControlStateReport, ProcessStartReport, ProcessCompletionReport, AlarmReport,
SpoolingReport, TraceSummaryReport. See Section 15.
13. DVs linked to completion
ProcessCompletionReport links RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec,
ProcessEndStatus, RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage to
CEID 5002. See Section 15.
14. START parameter requirements
START requires RecipeID; optional LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and
IDLE; invalid parameter returns S2F42 parameter error. See Section 16.
15. Mass filter/beam drift ALIDs
No ALID is assigned to MassFilterFault or BeamDrift. They are not applicable to ETCH-PRO-X100 unless explicitly
documented. Closest related alarms are GasFlowOutOfRange (1005) and RFPowerFault (1006). See Section 14.

5. Equipment Description and Operations
The ETCH-PRO-X100 is a plasma etching system used for semiconductor wafer processing. It executes recipe-driven
etch sequences in a controlled chamber using vacuum control, process gas delivery, RF power, plasma ignition,
endpoint monitoring, and post-process completion handling. The host interface supports production integration with
MES/CIM systems for data collection, alarms, remote control, recipes, and recovery from communication loss.
5.1 Plasma Etching Purpose
- Remove selected films or material layers from wafer surfaces using plasma chemistry and RF energy.
- Maintain process repeatability by monitoring chamber pressure, gas flow, RF power, temperature, plasma state,
endpoint status, and process duration.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$e5a8deb2-a61a-45f4-afc3-97e286f63665h
)}(h
}(hh@h}(hKhhhhhhhhhKhKuhX­␀␀- Maintain process repeatability by monitoring chamber pressure, gas flow, RF power, temperature, plasma state,
endpoint status, and process duration.
- Generate traceability records at lot, carrier, wafer, recipe, process start, plasma ignition, and process completion
points.

5.3 Host/MES Interface Purpose
- Establish a reliable SECS/GEM HSMS link for production automation.
- Provide status, trace, and event data for equipment and process characterization.
- Support alarms with S5F1/S5F2 set/clear notification and alarm list retrieval.
- Permit controlled remote operation via S2F41/S2F42 when in ON-LINE REMOTE.
- Manage process programs using S7 download/upload transactions.
- Spool alarm and event messages during communication loss and deliver them after recovery.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$fb328505-df9c-4838-a1ff-2b223e4e0c07h

6. SEMI Standards Supported
The ETCH-PRO-X100 host interface follows the SECS/GEM standards family. The system uses HSMS over TCP/IP as
the transport and SECS-II/GEM for application-level messages. SECS-I is referenced for historical SECS definitions but
is not the active physical communication path for this equipment.

7. HSMS Connection Settings
The ETCH-PRO-X100 operates in HSMS Passive mode. The equipment listens on TCP port 5011, and the fab host
initiates the connection. Device ID is 0 for the single logical device.

9.1 PPID and PPBODY Handling
The process program identifier (PPID) is represented by RecipeID / ActiveRecipe and is used to select the etch
process recipe. PPBODY is supported as an unformatted body through S7F3 process program download and
S7F5/S7F6 process program upload. The equipment validates the PPID, required recipe structure, chamber limits,
gas/RF setpoints, maximum process time, and endpoint configuration before accepting process execution.
Function
Message Pair
Behavior
Download recipe
S7F3/S7F4
Host sends PPID and PPBODY. ACKC7=0 indicates accepted.

This condensed message summary preserves the original ETCH-PRO-X100 manual content while keeping the revised
document extraction-friendly. Detailed SML examples are provided in Section 18.

10. State Models and State Reference Tables
Initial states: Default communication state on power-up is NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and
S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is OFF-LINE. Initial process state is IDLE.
10A. Communication State Reference
State ID
State Name
Description
COMM-0
DISABLED
SECS/GEM communication is disabled by configuration or operator action. Equipment
does not initiate or accept application messages.
COMM-1
NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING
Default communication state on power-up. TCP may be disconnected or HSMS not
selected; S1F13/S1F14 has not completed.
COMM-2
SELECTED / COMMUNICATING
HSMS Select is complete and S1F13/S1F14 establish communications has completed with
COMMACK=0.

10E. Process State Reference
State ID
State Name
Description
PROC-0
IDLE
Initial process state. Equipment is not processing, no active wafer in etch sequence, and START/INITIALIZE
may be accepted if in REMOTE.
PROC-1
SETUP
Recipe and material context are being validated; chamber preparation may start.
PROC-2
PROCESSING
Wafer etch is active; plasma, gas flow, RF power, pressure, and endpoint are monitored.
PROC-3
PAUSED
Processing is temporarily suspended by PAUSE or an interlock condition that permits resume.
PROC-4
COMPLETING
Etch sequence is ending, post-process purge/vent/robot handoff and result calculation are underway.
PROC-5
ERROR
Fault state caused by critical alarm, failed command, unsafe pressure/temperature, or unrecoverable
transfer error.

16. Remote Commands
START inconsistency resolved: START is documented as the host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Hosts may
send RCMD="START"; the equipment executes the INITIALIZE process-start path and reports command history as START
while mapping execution to INITIALIZE internally.
Command Name
Description
Parameters
START
Host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Starts process setup and
processing when accepted.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
INITIALIZE
Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
STOP
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
PAUSE
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
Optional: ReasonCode.

STOP
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
PAUSE
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
Optional: ReasonCode.
RESUME

Clears ERROR state after alarms are resolved and returns process state to

Optional: ChamberID, VentMode.
CLEAN_CHAMBER
Runs chamber clean recipe or predefined clean cycle.
Required: RecipeID or CleanRecipeID. Optional: ChamberID.

16.4 S2F42 Acknowledgement and Parameter Validation
Code / Field
Meaning
Typical Cause / Host Action
HCACK=0
Command accepted
Command will execute or has been queued. Monitor LastCommandStatus and CEIDs.
HCACK=1
Command does not exist
RCMD spelling mismatch or unsupported command. Use START, INITIALIZE, STOP,
PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER.
HCACK=2
Cannot perform now
Wrong process state, unresolved alarm, chamber not safe, or command conflict.
HCACK=3
At least one parameter invalid
CPNAME/CPVAL value is out of range, unsupported, or invalid type.
HCACK=4
Command will be performed with completion
signaled later
Used only if asynchronous command completion is site-configured.
HCACK=5
Rejected, already in desired condition
Example: RESUME when not PAUSED or RESET when already IDLE.
HCACK=6
Rejected in current control statehh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$573883b3-c161-45bf-8018-aea3ae440e4bh
)}(h
}(hj¬␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhKhK9uhXÅ␀␀HCACK=5
Rejected, already in desired condition
Example: RESUME when not PAUSED or RESET when already IDLE.
HCACK=6
Rejected in current control state
Equipment is not ON-LINE REMOTE. Request REMOTE/local authorization before retry.
Parameter error
S2F42 command parameter error list returned
Missing required RecipeID for START/INITIALIZE or invalid
ChamberID/CarrierID/WaferID.

Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,

Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
STOP
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
PAUSE
Optional: ReasonCode.
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.

19. Operational Scenarios
The scenarios below summarize the expected sequence and behavior for the most common ETCH-PRO-X100 host
integration tests.
Scenario
Expected Sequence / Result
Establish Communications
Host opens TCP connection to port 5011; HSMS Select succeeds; S1F13/S1F14 returns COMMACK=0; state becomes SELECTED /
COMMUNICATING.
Host synchronizes status
Host sends S1F3/S1F4 for current state, S2F33/S2F35/S2F37 to define/link/enable reports, and S5F3 to enable alarms.
Define/link/enable reports
Host defines RPTID 7004, links it to CEID 5002, and enables CEIDs 5001 and 5002.
Start lot/process
Host sends S2F41 START with RecipeID. START maps to INITIALIZE; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$d480de7e-bc79-4025-8712-693169d7da7ah
)}(h
}(hjF␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK$hKOuhX4␀␀Start lot/process
Host sends S2F41 START with RecipeID. START maps to INITIALIZE; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE.
Process completion
Equipment sends S6F11 CEID 5002 with ProcessCompletionReport; host replies S6F12 ACKC6=0.
Alarm set/clear
Equipment sends S5F1 with ALCD bit 7 set for SET and clear for CLEAR; host replies S5F2.
Remote command failure
Missing RecipeID, LOCAL control, non-IDLE process state, or unresolved alarm returns S2F42 nonzero HCACK/parameter error.
Spooling during communication loss
On TCP disconnect or timeout, spooling activates for configured streams/functions. Stored S5F1/S6F11 messages are delivered
after recovery using S6F23/S6F24.
Recovery from ERROR state
Host acknowledges alarm, waits for physical fault clear, sends RESET, and confirms ProcessState returns ERROR -> IDLE.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$483b0361-2afb-4149-a99c-197bdc126d48h

20.1 Required Question Answer Coverage
The following matrix confirms that the revised ETCH-PRO-X100 manual answers the 15 required extraction
questions.
Question
Answer / Manual Location
1. Tool type or model
Plasma Etching System, Model ETCH-PRO-X100, Tool ID EQP-5000. See Sections 1 and 4.
2. Protocol version
SECS/GEM over HSMS/HSMS-SS using SEMI E5, E30, E37, and E37.1; document Rev A. See Sections 1, 6, and 7.
3. Status variables for monitoring
Yes. SVs include ChamberPressure, ChamberTemperature, RFForwardPower, RFReflectedPower, GasFlowRate,
PlasmaState, EndpointStatus, and state variables. See Section 12.1.
4. Primary DVs related to processing
RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec, ProcessEndStatus,
RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage, EndpointResult. Seehh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$6e6993f7-c164-44bf-a861-577a9c4f0f1fh
)}(h

Section 12.2.
5. Critical CEIDs during lot start/end
5001 ProcessStarted and 5002 ProcessCompleted; carrier context uses 5200 CarrierLoaded and 5201
CarrierUnloaded. See Section 13.
6. Safety/fault alarms
ALIDs 1001-1015 include ChamberOverheat, VacuumPressureTooHigh, RFPowerFault, DoorInterlockOpen,
EmergencyStopActivated, WaferTransferError, and others. See Section 14.
7. Remote commands
START, INITIALIZE, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER. START is alias for
INITIALIZE. See Section 16.
8. States/transitions
Communication, control, and process state reference/transition tables are included. See Section 10.
9. Default communication state on power-up
NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is
OFF-LINE; process state is IDLE. See Section 10.
10. Process state machinehh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$942cac5c-ca2b-4f69-898a-4bb19b835d07h

OFF-LINE; process state is IDLE. See Section 10.
10. Process state machine
IDLE -> SETUP -> PROCESSING -> COMPLETING -> IDLE; PROCESSING -> PAUSED -> PROCESSING; PROCESSING ->
ERROR -> IDLE. See Section 10.
11. Spooling support/configuration
Spooling is supported; default enabled, buffer size 5000 messages, retention 24 hr, default streams/functions
include S5F1 and S6F11. See Section 11 and SML in Section 18.
12. Predefined reports
CommunicationStateReport, ControlStateReport, ProcessStartReport, ProcessCompletionReport, AlarmReport,
SpoolingReport, TraceSummaryReport. See Section 15.
13. DVs linked to completion
ProcessCompletionReport links RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec,
ProcessEndStatus, RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage to
CEID 5002. See Section 15.

SECS/GEM Equipment Interface Manual - ETCH-PRO-X100
Rev A | CONFIDENTIAL
PRJ-FEM-001 | Tool ID EQP-5000 | Fab-Alpha
Page 5
5. Equipment Description and Operations
The ETCH-PRO-X100 is a plasma etching system used for semiconductor wafer processing. It executes recipe-driven
etch sequences in a controlled chamber using vacuum control, process gas delivery, RF power, plasma ignition,
endpoint monitoring, and post-process completion handling. The host interface supports production integration with
MES/CIM systems for data collection, alarms, remote control, recipes, and recovery from communication loss.
5.1 Plasma Etching Purpose
- Remove selected films or material layers from wafer surfaces using plasma chemistry and RF energy.
- Maintain process repeatability by monitoring chamber pressure, gas flow, RF power, temperature, plasma state,
endpoint status, and process duration.
- Generate traceability records at lot, carrier, wafer, recipe, process start, plasma ignition, and process completion
points.
5.2 Wafer Processing Flow
Step
Operation
Host Interface Impact
1
Carrier loaded and material context
identified
CEID 5200 CarrierLoaded can report CarrierID, LotID, WaferID, and status.
2
Recipe/PPID selected or downloaded
S7F3/S7F4 may download process program; ActiveRecipe and RecipeID updated.
3
Host sends START alias or INITIALIZE
S2F41 command accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE with required RecipeID.
4
Setup and chamber preparation
ProcessState moves IDLE -> SETUP; pressure/gas/RF prerequisites checked.
5
Plasma process executes
ProcessState PROCESSING; CEID 5100 PlasmaIgnition; SVs and trace data available.
6
Completion and result calculation
CEID 5002 ProcessCompleted; ProcessCompletionReport includes completion DVs.
7
Carrier unload or next wafer
CEID 5201 CarrierUnloaded or next wafer sequence.
5.3 Host/MES Interface Purpose
- Establish a reliable SECS/GEM HSMS link for production automation.
- Provide status, trace, and event data for equipment and process characterization.
- Support alarms with S5F1/S5F2 set/clear notification and alarm list retrieval.
- Permit controlled remote operation via S2F41/S2F42 when in ON-LINE REMOTE.
- Manage process programs using S7 download/upload transactions.
- Spool alarm and event messages during communication loss and deliver them after recovery.

SECS/GEM Equipment Interface Manual - ETCH-PRO-X100
Rev A | CONFIDENTIAL
PRJ-FEM-001 | Tool ID EQP-5000 | Fab-Alpha
Page 6
6. SEMI Standards Supported
The ETCH-PRO-X100 host interface follows the SECS/GEM standards family. The system uses HSMS over TCP/IP as
the transport and SECS-II/GEM for application-level messages. SECS-I is referenced for historical SECS definitions but
is not the active physical communication path for this equipment.
Standard
Revision
Description
SEMI E4
0712 / applicable release
SEMI Equipment Communications Standard 1 Message Transfer (SECS-I). Referenced for SECS concepts;
ETCH-PRO-X100 uses HSMS, not serial SECS-I.
SEMI E5
0219 / applicable release
SECS-II message content, stream/function definitions, and data item encoding.
SEMI E30
0717 / applicable release
Generic Model for Communications and Control of Manufacturing Equipment (GEM).
SEMI E37
1018 / applicable release
High-Speed Message Services (HSMS) over TCP/IP.
SEMI E37.1
0702 / applicable release
High-Speed Message Services Single Session Mode (HSMS-SS).
SEMI E10
Applicable release
Definition and measurement of equipment reliability, availability, and maintainability.
SEMI E116
Applicable release
Equipment performance tracking reference; used for availability and status context when required by site.
SEMI E145
Applicable release
Units and symbols for semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Protocol statement: ETCH-PRO-X100 supports SECS/GEM over HSMS single-session operation. The implemented host
interface is documented as Rev A for this equipment manual.

SECS/GEM Equipment Interface Manual - ETCH-PRO-X100

7. HSMS Connection Settings
The ETCH-PRO-X100 operates in HSMS Passive mode. The equipment listens on TCP port 5011, and the fab host
initiates the connection. Device ID is 0 for the single logical device.

8.1 Compliance Summary
The ETCH-PRO-X100 implements the required host communication, state model, data collection, alarm, control,
clock, and remote command functions needed for a production SECS/GEM integration. Additional functions such as
trace data, dynamic event report configuration, limits monitoring, process program management, equipment
terminal services, and spooling are documented for characterization and host qualification.
8.2 Overall GEM Compliance Status
Overall GEM Compliance Status: Supported for the documented ETCH-PRO-X100 Rev A interface. Some capabilities, such as
material movement, are limited to carrier/wafer event reporting and do not claim complete SEMI E87 carrier management.

9.1 PPID and PPBODY Handling
The process program identifier (PPID) is represented by RecipeID / ActiveRecipe and is used to select the etch
process recipe. PPBODY is supported as an unformatted body through S7F3 process program download and
S7F5/S7F6 process program upload. The equipment validates the PPID, required recipe structure, chamber limits,
gas/RF setpoints, maximum process time, and endpoint configuration before accepting process execution.
Function
Message Pair
Behavior
Download recipe
S7F3/S7F4
Host sends PPID and PPBODY. ACKC7=0 indicates accepted.
Upload recipe
S7F5/S7F6
Host requests PPID; equipment returns PPBODY if stored.
Delete recipe
S7F17/S7F18
Host requests deletion; equipment rejects active recipe deletion.
Directory request
S7F19/S7F20
Equipment returns current process program directory.

10. State Models and State Reference Tables
Initial states: Default communication state on power-up is NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and
S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is OFF-LINE. Initial process state is IDLE.
10A. Communication State Reference

Description

does not initiate or accept application messages.

Default communication state on power-up. TCP may be disconnected or HSMS not
selected; S1F13/S1F14 has not completed.
COMM-2
SELECTED / COMMUNICATING
HSMS Select is complete and S1F13/S1F14 establish communications has completed with
COMMACK=0.

10E. Process State Reference
State ID
State Name
Description
PROC-0
IDLE
Initial process state. Equipment is not processing, no active wafer in etch sequence, and START/INITIALIZE
may be accepted if in REMOTE.
PROC-1
SETUP
Recipe and material context are being validated; chamber preparation may start.
PROC-2
PROCESSING
Wafer etch is active; plasma, gas flow, RF power, pressure, and endpoint are monitored.
PROC-3
PAUSED
Processing is temporarily suspended by PAUSE or an interlock condition that permits resume.
PROC-4
COMPLETING
Etch sequence is ending, post-process purge/vent/robot handoff and result calculation are underway.
PROC-5
ERROR
Fault state caused by critical alarm, failed command, unsafe pressure/temperature, or unrecoverable
transfer error.

Transition
From State
To State
Trigger / Condition
P-T1
IDLE
SETUP

P-T2
SETUP
PROCESSING
Recipe validated, chamber ready, wafer/carrier context accepted, RF/gas sequence
begins.
P-T3
PROCESSING
COMPLETING
Etch endpoint reached, recipe timer elapsed, or normal process stop criteria met.
P-T4
COMPLETING
IDLE
Post-process clean-up complete and CEID 5002 ProcessCompleted emitted.
P-T5
PROCESSING
PAUSED
Host sends PAUSE or recoverable interlock/pause condition occurs.
P-T6
PAUSED
PROCESSING
Host sends RESUME and process conditions are valid.
P-T7
PROCESSING

Critical alarm such as ChamberOverheat, VacuumPressureTooHigh, RFPowerFault,

P-T8
ERROR
IDLE
Fault cleared and host/operator sends RESET; reset accepted only after physical
alarm condition is resolved.

14. Alarm Verification
The ETCH-PRO-X100 defines ALID 1001-1015. All alarms are reported using S5F1 when enabled. The ALCD alarm
code uses bit 7 to indicate set/clear: bit 7 set indicates alarm SET; bit 7 clear indicates alarm CLEAR.
Alarm ID
Alarm Code
Alarm Name
Severity
Description
1001
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
ChamberOverheat
Critical
Chamber temperature exceeded maximum safe limit.
1002
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
RobotNotHomed
Warning
Wafer transfer robot has not returned to home position.
1003
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
VacuumPressureTooHigh
Critical
Chamber vacuum pressure exceeded maximum allowed value.
1004
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR
VacuumPumpFailure
Warning
Vacuum pump failed, degraded, or did not reach expected vacuum
condition.
1005
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Warning
Measured process gas flow is outside configured tolerance.
1006
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Critical
RF generator, match network, or forward/reflected RF power fault
detected during processing.
1007
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Warning
Cooling water temperature exceeded configured limit.
1008
0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

0x81 SET / 0x01
CLEAR

Warning
Scheduled maintenance interval reached.
Mass filter / beam drift applicability: No ALID is assigned to MassFilterFault. No ALID is assigned to BeamDrift. These
conditions are not applicable to ETCH-PRO-X100 unless explicitly documented by a future equipment revision. Closest
related ETCH-PRO alarms are GasFlowOutOfRange (ALID 1005) and RFPowerFault (ALID 1006).
14.1 Alarm Recovery Procedures
Alarm / Condition
Equipment Action
Host Recovery Action
ChamberOverheat (1001)
Immediate process halt, RF off, transition to ERROR.
Acknowledge S5F1, investigate temperature root cause, wait for
clear, send RESET.
VacuumPressureTooHigh (1003)
Immediate process halt or safe stop, transition to ERROR.
Acknowledge, verify vacuum/pump state, clear physical
condition, send RESET.
RFPowerFault (1006)
RF output disabled; process abort may be required.
Acknowledge, verify generator/match network, restart only after
RESET or safe idle.
DoorInterlockOpen (1009)
Process inhibited or halted; safety interlock enforced.
Acknowledge and keep equipment blocked until door interlock is
restored.
EmergencyStopActivated (1010)
All motion/process activity stopped; ERROR state.
Acknowledge, require operator reset at tool, then send RESET
only after E-stop release.
WaferTransferError (1013)
Robot/wafer transfer stops; wafer status requires operator
verification.
Acknowledge, resolve transfer condition, verify wafer location,
send RESET if permitted.
Warning alarms
(1002,1004,1005,1007,1008,1011,1012,1014,1015)
Process may continue or pause depending on recipe/site
policy.
Acknowledge, log, and decide whether to STOP, allow
continuation, or schedule maintenance.

16. Remote Commands
START inconsistency resolved: START is documented as the host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Hosts may
send RCMD="START"; the equipment executes the INITIALIZE process-start path and reports command history as START
while mapping execution to INITIALIZE internally.
Command Name
Description
Parameters
START
Host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Starts process setup and
processing when accepted.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
INITIALIZE
Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
STOP
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
PAUSE
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
Optional: ReasonCode.
RESUME
Resumes process from PAUSED state after conditions are valid.
No required parameters. Optional: ReasonCode.
RESET
Clears ERROR state after alarms are resolved and returns process state to
IDLE.
Optional: ResetMode, ReasonCode.
PUMP_DOWN
Starts chamber pump-down sequence when idle and interlocks are safe.
Optional: ChamberID, TargetPressure.
VENT
Starts chamber vent sequence when idle or maintenance mode allows.
Optional: ChamberID, VentMode.
CLEAN_CHAMBER
Runs chamber clean recipe or predefined clean cycle.
Required: RecipeID or CleanRecipeID. Optional: ChamberID.
16.1 START Parameter Requirements
Item
Requirement
Required parameters
RecipeID
Optional parameters
LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID
Allowed state
Control state must be ON-LINE REMOTE and process state must be IDLE
Success behavior
S2F42 HCACK=0; emits CEID 5001 ProcessStarted and later CEID 5002 ProcessCompleted
Invalid parameter behavior
S2F42 parameter error; command rejected and no process state transition occurs
START alias rule
START is accepted as host-facing alias for INITIALIZE; INITIALIZE remains the canonical equipment command

16.4 S2F42 Acknowledgement and Parameter Validation
Code / Field
Meaning
Typical Cause / Host Action
HCACK=0
Command accepted
Command will execute or has been queued. Monitor LastCommandStatus and CEIDs.
HCACK=1
Command does not exist
RCMD spelling mismatch or unsupported command. Use START, INITIALIZE, STOP,
PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER.
HCACK=2
Cannot perform now
Wrong process state, unresolved alarm, chamber not safe, or command conflict.
HCACK=3
At least one parameter invalid
CPNAME/CPVAL value is out of range, unsupported, or invalid type.
HCACK=4
Command will be performed with completion
signaled later
Used only if asynchronous command completion is site-configured.
HCACK=5
Rejected, already in desired condition
Example: RESUME when not PAUSED or RESET when already IDLE.
HCACK=6
Rejected in current control state
Equipment is not ON-LINE REMOTE. Request REMOTE/local authorization before retry.
Parameter error
S2F42 command parameter error list returned
Missing required RecipeID for START/INITIALIZE or invalid
ChamberID/CarrierID/WaferID.

19. Operational Scenarios
The scenarios below summarize the expected sequence and behavior for the most common ETCH-PRO-X100 host
integration tests.
Scenario
Expected Sequence / Result
Establish Communications
Host opens TCP connection to port 5011; HSMS Select succeeds; S1F13/S1F14 returns COMMACK=0; state becomes SELECTED /
COMMUNICATING.
Host synchronizes status
Host sends S1F3/S1F4 for current state, S2F33/S2F35/S2F37 to define/link/enable reports, and S5F3 to enable alarms.
Define/link/enable reports
Host defines RPTID 7004, links it to CEID 5002, and enables CEIDs 5001 and 5002.
Start lot/process
Host sends S2F41 START with RecipeID. START maps to INITIALIZE; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE.
Process completion
Equipment sends S6F11 CEID 5002 with ProcessCompletionReport; host replies S6F12 ACKC6=0.
Alarm set/clear
Equipment sends S5F1 with ALCD bit 7 set for SET and clear for CLEAR; host replies S5F2.
Remote command failure
Missing RecipeID, LOCAL control, non-IDLE process state, or unresolved alarm returns S2F42 nonzero HCACK/parameter error.
Spooling during communication loss
On TCP disconnect or timeout, spooling activates for configured streams/functions. Stored S5F1/S6F11 messages are delivered
after recovery using S6F23/S6F24.
Recovery from ERROR state
Host acknowledges alarm, waits for physical fault clear, sends RESET, and confirms ProcessState returns ERROR -> IDLE.

20.1 Required Question Answer Coverage
The following matrix confirms that the revised ETCH-PRO-X100 manual answers the 15 required extraction
questions.
Question
Answer / Manual Location
1. Tool type or model
Plasma Etching System, Model ETCH-PRO-X100, Tool ID EQP-5000. See Sections 1 and 4.
2. Protocol version
SECS/GEM over HSMS/HSMS-SS using SEMI E5, E30, E37, and E37.1; document Rev A. See Sections 1, 6, and 7.
3. Status variables for monitoring
Yes. SVs include ChamberPressure, ChamberTemperature, RFForwardPower, RFReflectedPower, GasFlowRate,
PlasmaState, EndpointStatus, and state variables. See Section 12.1.
4. Primary DVs related to processing
RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec, ProcessEndStatus,
RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage, EndpointResult. See
Section 12.2.
5. Critical CEIDs during lot start/end
5001 ProcessStarted and 5002 ProcessCompleted; carrier context uses 5200 CarrierLoaded and 5201
CarrierUnloaded. See Section 13.
6. Safety/fault alarms
ALIDs 1001-1015 include ChamberOverheat, VacuumPressureTooHigh, RFPowerFault, DoorInterlockOpen,
EmergencyStopActivated, WaferTransferError, and others. See Section 14.
7. Remote commands
START, INITIALIZE, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER. START is alias for
INITIALIZE. See Section 16.
8. States/transitions
Communication, control, and process state reference/transition tables are included. See Section 10.
9. Default communication state on power-up
NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is
OFF-LINE; process state is IDLE. See Section 10.
10. Process state machine
IDLE -> SETUP -> PROCESSING -> COMPLETING -> IDLE; PROCESSING -> PAUSED -> PROCESSING; PROCESSING ->
ERROR -> IDLE. See Section 10.
11. Spooling support/configuration
Spooling is supported; default enabled, buffer size 5000 messages, retention 24 hr, default streams/functions
include S5F1 and S6F11. See Section 11 and SML in Section 18.
12. Predefined reports
CommunicationStateReport, ControlStateReport, ProcessStartReport, ProcessCompletionReport, AlarmReport,
SpoolingReport, TraceSummaryReport. See Section 15.
13. DVs linked to completion
ProcessCompletionReport links RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec,
ProcessEndStatus, RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage to
CEID 5002. See Section 15.
14. START parameter requirements
START requires RecipeID; optional LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and
IDLE; invalid parameter returns S2F42 parameter error. See Section 16.
15. Mass filter/beam drift ALIDs
No ALID is assigned to MassFilterFault or BeamDrift. They are not applicable to ETCH-PRO-X100 unless explicitly
documented. Closest related alarms are GasFlowOutOfRange (1005) and RFPowerFault (1006). See Section 14.

// ========================================================================
// EXECUTABLE SML MACRO TEST SCRIPT FOR: EQP-5000

// --- S1F1: Are You There --- 
SEND S1F1 W.
RECEIVE S1F2 <L [2] <A> <A>>. // Accepts any tool model/version string

// --- S1F13: Establish Communication --- 
SEND S1F13 W
  <L [0]>
.
RECEIVE S1F14
  <L [2]
    <B 00>
    <L [2]
      <A> // Tool Model Placeholder
      <A> // Software Rev Placeholder
    >
  >
.

// --- S1F11: Request Specific Status Variables ---
SEND S1F11 W
  <L [20]
    <U4 10001> <U4 10002> <U4 10003> <U4 10004> <U4 10005>
    <U4 10006> <U4 10007> <U4 10008> <U4 10009> <U4 10010>
    <U4 10011> <U4 10012> <U4 10013> <U4 10014> <U4 10015>
    <U4 10016> <U4 10017> <U4 10018> <U4 10019> <U4 10020>
  >
.
RECEIVE S1F12
  <L [20] <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V>> // Expects 20 values back
.

// --- S1F21: Request Specific Data Variables ---
SEND S1F21 W
  <L [20]
    <U4 3001> <U4 3002> <U4 3003> <U4 3004> <U4 3005>
    <U4 3007> <U4 3016> <U4 3017> <U4 3018> <U4 3019>
    <U4 3020> <U4 3021> <U4 3022> <U4 3023> <U4 3024>
    <U4 1> <U4 2> <U4 3> <U4 4> <U4 5>
  >
.
RECEIVE S1F22
  <L [20] <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V> <V>>
.

// --- S2F33: Define Reports ---
SEND S2F33 W
  <L [2]
    <U4 1>                    * DATAID
    <L [4]
      <L [2]
        <U4 1>                * RPTID (Process Start Report)
        <L [13]
          <U4 3001> <U4 3002> <U4 3003> <U4 1> <U4 2> <U4 3> <U4 4> 
          <U4 5> <U4 6> <U4 7> <U4 8> <U4 10003> <U4 10004>
        >
      >
      <L [2]
        <U4 2>                * RPTID (Alarm and Error Report)
        <L [8]
          <U4 10007> <U4 10008> <U4 10009> <U4 10010> <U4 10011> 
          <U4 10012> <U4 10013> <U4 10014>
        >
      >
      <L [2]
        <U4 3>                * RPTID (Equipment Status Report)
        <L [12]
          <U4 10001> <U4 10002> <U4 10003> <U4 10004> <U4 10005> <U4 10006> 
          <U4 10015> <U4 10016> <U4 10017> <U4 10018> <U4 10019> <U4 10020>
        >
      >
      <L [2]
        <U4 4>                * RPTID (Carrier Management Report)
        <L [10]
          <U4 1> <U4 2> <U4 3> <U4 4> <U4 5> <U4 6> <U4 7> <U4 8> 
          <U4 10006> <U4 3004>
        >
      >
    >
  >
.
RECEIVE S2F34
  <B 00>
.

// --- S2F35: Link Reports to Events ---
SEND S2F35 W
  <L [2]
    <U4 1>                    * DATAID
    <L [2]
      <L [2]
        <U4 5001>             * CEID (ProcessStarted)
        <L [1] <U4 1>>        * Linked to RPTID 1

    >

  <B 00>
.

  <L [14]
    <U4 5001> <U4 5002> <U4 5100> <U4 5200> <U4 5201> <U4 5300> <U4 5301> 
    <U4 5302> <U4 5303> <U4 5400> <U4 5500> <U4 5501> <U4 5600> <U4 5601>

5. Equipment Description and Operations
The ETCH-PRO-X100 is a plasma etching system used for semiconductor wafer processing. It executes recipe-driven
etch sequences in a controlled chamber using vacuum control, process gas delivery, RF power, plasma ignition,
endpoint monitoring, and post-process completion handling. The host interface supports production integration with
MES/CIM systems for data collection, alarms, remote control, recipes, and recovery from communication loss.
5.1 Plasma Etching Purpose
- Remove selected films or material layers from wafer surfaces using plasma chemistry and RF energy.
- Maintain process repeatability by monitoring chamber pressure, gas flow, RF power, temperature, plasma state,
endpoint status, and process duration.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$864e833c-c326-4eac-8ba1-762fdf05d9bbh
)}(h
}(hh@h}(hKhhhhhhhhhKhKuhX­␀␀- Maintain process repeatability by monitoring chamber pressure, gas flow, RF power, temperature, plasma state,
endpoint status, and process duration.
- Generate traceability records at lot, carrier, wafer, recipe, process start, plasma ignition, and process completion
points.

5.3 Host/MES Interface Purpose
- Establish a reliable SECS/GEM HSMS link for production automation.
- Provide status, trace, and event data for equipment and process characterization.
- Support alarms with S5F1/S5F2 set/clear notification and alarm list retrieval.
- Permit controlled remote operation via S2F41/S2F42 when in ON-LINE REMOTE.
- Manage process programs using S7 download/upload transactions.
- Spool alarm and event messages during communication loss and deliver them after recovery.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$6eb62eff-02c2-4a7f-8270-ab42657bcb12h

6. SEMI Standards Supported
The ETCH-PRO-X100 host interface follows the SECS/GEM standards family. The system uses HSMS over TCP/IP as
the transport and SECS-II/GEM for application-level messages. SECS-I is referenced for historical SECS definitions but
is not the active physical communication path for this equipment.

7. HSMS Connection Settings
The ETCH-PRO-X100 operates in HSMS Passive mode. The equipment listens on TCP port 5011, and the fab host
initiates the connection. Device ID is 0 for the single logical device.

9.1 PPID and PPBODY Handling
The process program identifier (PPID) is represented by RecipeID / ActiveRecipe and is used to select the etch
process recipe. PPBODY is supported as an unformatted body through S7F3 process program download and
S7F5/S7F6 process program upload. The equipment validates the PPID, required recipe structure, chamber limits,
gas/RF setpoints, maximum process time, and endpoint configuration before accepting process execution.
Function
Message Pair
Behavior
Download recipe
S7F3/S7F4
Host sends PPID and PPBODY. ACKC7=0 indicates accepted.

10. State Models and State Reference Tables
Initial states: Default communication state on power-up is NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and
S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is OFF-LINE. Initial process state is IDLE.
10A. Communication State Reference
State ID
State Name
Description
COMM-0
DISABLED
SECS/GEM communication is disabled by configuration or operator action. Equipment
does not initiate or accept application messages.
COMM-1
NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING
Default communication state on power-up. TCP may be disconnected or HSMS not
selected; S1F13/S1F14 has not completed.
COMM-2
SELECTED / COMMUNICATING
HSMS Select is complete and S1F13/S1F14 establish communications has completed with
COMMACK=0.

10E. Process State Reference
State ID
State Name
Description
PROC-0
IDLE
Initial process state. Equipment is not processing, no active wafer in etch sequence, and START/INITIALIZE
may be accepted if in REMOTE.
PROC-1
SETUP
Recipe and material context are being validated; chamber preparation may start.
PROC-2
PROCESSING
Wafer etch is active; plasma, gas flow, RF power, pressure, and endpoint are monitored.
PROC-3
PAUSED
Processing is temporarily suspended by PAUSE or an interlock condition that permits resume.
PROC-4
COMPLETING
Etch sequence is ending, post-process purge/vent/robot handoff and result calculation are underway.
PROC-5
ERROR
Fault state caused by critical alarm, failed command, unsafe pressure/temperature, or unrecoverable
transfer error.

16. Remote Commands
START inconsistency resolved: START is documented as the host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Hosts may
send RCMD="START"; the equipment executes the INITIALIZE process-start path and reports command history as START
while mapping execution to INITIALIZE internally.
Command Name
Description
Parameters
START
Host-facing command alias for RCMD=INITIALIZE. Starts process setup and
processing when accepted.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
INITIALIZE
Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
STOP
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
PAUSE
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
Optional: ReasonCode.

STOP
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
PAUSE
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
Optional: ReasonCode.
RESUME
Resumes process from PAUSED state after conditions are valid.
No required parameters. Optional: ReasonCode.
RESET
Clears ERROR state after alarms are resolved and returns process state to
IDLE.
Optional: ResetMode, ReasonCode.
PUMP_DOWN
Starts chamber pump-down sequence when idle and interlocks are safe.

VENT
Starts chamber vent sequence when idle or maintenance mode allows.
Optional: ChamberID, VentMode.
CLEAN_CHAMBER
Runs chamber clean recipe or predefined clean cycle.
Required: RecipeID or CleanRecipeID. Optional: ChamberID.

16.4 S2F42 Acknowledgement and Parameter Validation
Code / Field
Meaning
Typical Cause / Host Action
HCACK=0
Command accepted
Command will execute or has been queued. Monitor LastCommandStatus and CEIDs.
HCACK=1
Command does not exist
RCMD spelling mismatch or unsupported command. Use START, INITIALIZE, STOP,
PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER.
HCACK=2
Cannot perform now
Wrong process state, unresolved alarm, chamber not safe, or command conflict.
HCACK=3
At least one parameter invalid
CPNAME/CPVAL value is out of range, unsupported, or invalid type.
HCACK=4
Command will be performed with completion
signaled later
Used only if asynchronous command completion is site-configured.
HCACK=5
Rejected, already in desired condition
Example: RESUME when not PAUSED or RESET when already IDLE.
HCACK=6
Rejected in current control statehh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$5c664c9c-c00d-46dd-8823-24d450f71d41h
)}(h
}(hj¬␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhKhK9uhXÅ␀␀HCACK=5
Rejected, already in desired condition
Example: RESUME when not PAUSED or RESET when already IDLE.
HCACK=6
Rejected in current control state
Equipment is not ON-LINE REMOTE. Request REMOTE/local authorization before retry.
Parameter error
S2F42 command parameter error list returned
Missing required RecipeID for START/INITIALIZE or invalid
ChamberID/CarrierID/WaferID.

Description

Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,

Required: RecipeID. Optional: LotID, WaferID, CarrierID,
ChamberID.
Canonical ETCH-PRO command that initializes and starts the process
sequence. START maps to this command.
STOP
Optional: StopMode, ReasonCode.
Stops or aborts active process according to safe-stop policy.
PAUSE
Optional: ReasonCode.
Pauses active process if current step supports pause.
RESUME

Resumes process from PAUSED state after conditions are valid.

19. Operational Scenarios
The scenarios below summarize the expected sequence and behavior for the most common ETCH-PRO-X100 host
integration tests.
Scenario
Expected Sequence / Result
Establish Communications
Host opens TCP connection to port 5011; HSMS Select succeeds; S1F13/S1F14 returns COMMACK=0; state becomes SELECTED /
COMMUNICATING.
Host synchronizes status
Host sends S1F3/S1F4 for current state, S2F33/S2F35/S2F37 to define/link/enable reports, and S5F3 to enable alarms.
Define/link/enable reports
Host defines RPTID 7004, links it to CEID 5002, and enables CEIDs 5001 and 5002.
Start lot/process
Host sends S2F41 START with RecipeID. START maps to INITIALIZE; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$1e2167a0-d7b1-4e1d-83f4-ec30d9bbd819h

}(hjF␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK$hKOuhX4␀␀Start lot/process
Host sends S2F41 START with RecipeID. START maps to INITIALIZE; accepted only in ON-LINE REMOTE and IDLE.
Process completion
Equipment sends S6F11 CEID 5002 with ProcessCompletionReport; host replies S6F12 ACKC6=0.
Alarm set/clear
Equipment sends S5F1 with ALCD bit 7 set for SET and clear for CLEAR; host replies S5F2.
Remote command failure
Missing RecipeID, LOCAL control, non-IDLE process state, or unresolved alarm returns S2F42 nonzero HCACK/parameter error.
Spooling during communication loss
On TCP disconnect or timeout, spooling activates for configured streams/functions. Stored S5F1/S6F11 messages are delivered
after recovery using S6F23/S6F24.
Recovery from ERROR state
Host acknowledges alarm, waits for physical fault clear, sends RESET, and confirms ProcessState returns ERROR -> IDLE.hh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$484975c4-d55c-486a-89e7-37ea7b804403h

20.1 Required Question Answer Coverage
The following matrix confirms that the revised ETCH-PRO-X100 manual answers the 15 required extraction
questions.
Question
Answer / Manual Location
1. Tool type or model
Plasma Etching System, Model ETCH-PRO-X100, Tool ID EQP-5000. See Sections 1 and 4.
2. Protocol version
SECS/GEM over HSMS/HSMS-SS using SEMI E5, E30, E37, and E37.1; document Rev A. See Sections 1, 6, and 7.
3. Status variables for monitoring
Yes. SVs include ChamberPressure, ChamberTemperature, RFForwardPower, RFReflectedPower, GasFlowRate,
PlasmaState, EndpointStatus, and state variables. See Section 12.1.
4. Primary DVs related to processing
RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, ChamberID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec, ProcessEndStatus,
RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage, EndpointResult. Seehh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$e71253e3-2439-44dd-a217-a73ac085d78ah
)}(h
}(hjb␀␀h}(hKhhhhhhhhhK&hKSuhXÃ␀␀RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage, EndpointResult. See
Section 12.2.
5. Critical CEIDs during lot start/end
5001 ProcessStarted and 5002 ProcessCompleted; carrier context uses 5200 CarrierLoaded and 5201
CarrierUnloaded. See Section 13.
6. Safety/fault alarms
ALIDs 1001-1015 include ChamberOverheat, VacuumPressureTooHigh, RFPowerFault, DoorInterlockOpen,
EmergencyStopActivated, WaferTransferError, and others. See Section 14.
7. Remote commands
START, INITIALIZE, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME, RESET, PUMP_DOWN, VENT, CLEAN_CHAMBER. START is alias for
INITIALIZE. See Section 16.
8. States/transitions
Communication, control, and process state reference/transition tables are included. See Section 10.
9. Default communication state on power-up
NOT SELECTED / NOT COMMUNICATING until HSMS Select and S1F13/S1F14 complete. Initial control state is
OFF-LINE; process state is IDLE. See Section 10.
10. Process state machinehh	uh Nh!(hhhh#Nub$534081f1-bb83-498f-b3e2-1fe227e4ba3dh
)}(h

OFF-LINE; process state is IDLE. See Section 10.
10. Process state machine
IDLE -> SETUP -> PROCESSING -> COMPLETING -> IDLE; PROCESSING -> PAUSED -> PROCESSING; PROCESSING ->
ERROR -> IDLE. See Section 10.
11. Spooling support/configuration
Spooling is supported; default enabled, buffer size 5000 messages, retention 24 hr, default streams/functions
include S5F1 and S6F11. See Section 11 and SML in Section 18.
12. Predefined reports
CommunicationStateReport, ControlStateReport, ProcessStartReport, ProcessCompletionReport, AlarmReport,
SpoolingReport, TraceSummaryReport. See Section 15.
13. DVs linked to completion
ProcessCompletionReport links RecipeID, LotID, WaferID, CarrierID, EtchTime, EtchDepth, ProcessDurationSec,
ProcessEndStatus, RFPowerAverage, GasFlowAverage, ChamberPressureAverage, ChamberTemperatureAverage to
CEID 5002. See Section 15.

Chapter 1 — Introduction
1.1 Purpose and Scope
This manual describes the operation, architecture, and SECS/GEM host interface of the IMP-HE2000 High-Energy
Medium-Current Ion Implanter manufactured by PrecisionBeam Technologies. It covers equipment subsystems,
process workflows, state machine behaviour, alarm handling, and remote command capabilities. For all tabular data —
including variable IDs, event codes, alarm definitions, report structures, and state transitions — refer to the companion
workbook: IMP_HE2000_Variable_Tables.xlsx.
1.2 How to Use This Manual
This manual is the prose companion to the Variable Tables workbook. The manual explains HOW the equipment
works and WHY variables/events/alarms exist. The workbook provides the WHAT — exact IDs, types, ranges, and
linkages. Together they form the complete SECS/GEM Interface Control Document (ICD).
1.3 Companion Documents
The following companion documents should be read in conjunction with this manual:
• IMP_HE2000_Variable_Tables.xlsx — All variable, event, alarm, report, and command tables.
• IMP-HE2000-GEM-ICD-001 Rev A — Combined engineering specification (future release).
1.4 Terminology and Abbreviations
AMU (Atomic Mass Unit): The unit of measurement used to specify the mass of ions. It is critical in mass
spectrometry and ion beam mass analysis to ensure only the desired dopant species is selected and accelerated
toward the wafer.
AsHI (Arsine): A toxic process gas used as a precursor to supply Arsenic (As) ions for n-type doping of silicon
substrates.
BFI (Boron Trifluoride): A process gas commonly used to supply Boron (B) ions for p-type doping in semiconductor
processing.
CEID (Collection Event ID): A unique numeric identifier representing an equipment event that the host can subscribe
to, such as a process step starting, wafer loading, or status transition.
DV / DVID (Data Variable / Data Variable ID): A dynamic variable whose value is updated only during or upon
completion of specific events (e.g., post-implant wafer results).
EC (Equipment Constant): A user-configurable setpoint or operational parameter stored in the equipment controller
that governs local tool behaviour and can be modified by the host.
GEM (Generic Equipment Model): The SEMI E30 standard defining a generic model for communications and control
of manufacturing equipment by a host computer in a semiconductor fab.
HSMS (High-Speed Message Services): The SEMI E37 standard defining the TCP/IP-based transport layer protocol
used to transmit SECS-II messages between the equipment and the host.
keV (kilo-electron-Volt): A unit of energy representing the kinetic energy gained by an electron accelerating through a
potential difference of one thousand volts. It is the standard unit for specifying ion beam energy.
MFC (Mass Flow Controller): An active device used to precisely measure and control the flow rate of process gases
into the plasma arc chamber of the ion source.

IMP-HE2000 SECS/GEM User Manual  |  Revision A  |  PrecisionBeam Technologies
Page 5
PHI (Phosphine): A toxic process gas used to supply Phosphorus (P) ions for n-type doping in silicon wafers.
RCMD (Remote Command): A host-initiated instruction sent to the equipment to trigger a physical or logical change
(e.g., START_IMPLANT, ABORT_IMPLANT).
RPT / RPTID (Report / Report ID): A grouping of status or data variables defined by the host and linked to collection
events for structured data collection.
SECS-II (SEMI Equipment Communications Standard 2): The SEMI E5 standard defining the message structure
and semantic content exchanged between the host and the tool over HSMS.
SV / SVID (Status Variable / Status Variable ID): A continuous, real-time status variable representing equipment
parameters that can be read or polled at any time.
VID (Variable ID): A generic term referencing any status variable (SVID) or data variable (DVID).
1.5 Referenced Standards
The IMP-HE2000 SECS/GEM interface complies with the following industry standards:
• SEMI E5 — SECS-II Message Content Standard
• SEMI E30 — Generic Equipment Model (GEM) Standard
• SEMI E37 — High-Speed SECS Message Services (HSMS) Standard
• SEMI E10 — Equipment Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM)
• SEMI E40 — Standard for Processing Management
• SEMI E90 — Standard for Substrate Tracking
